definition_zh: 抛弃；遗弃；放弃；弃置；放任
definition_en: to leave a person, place, or thing behind for good, or to give up a plan, promise, or feeling completely
core_image: 一只手张开，放掉了原本紧紧握着的东西
scene: 深夜的旧宅只剩一盏灯，孩子的行李还摆在门口，车却已经开走。The family had to abandon the house when the river rose above the bridge.
sceneCN: 这里 abandon 指把住处丢下不管（第 1 个义项：弃置地方）；句意为河水漫过桥面时，一家人不得不弃屋离开。

pos.zh: 放任，仅见于短语 with abandon

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「遗弃；放弃；弃置」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「被遗弃的；废弃的」
由本词与 -ware 合成，义为「已停止维护、无人支持的软件」

senses.title: To leave a place and never return
senses.definition: to leave a house, town, or piece of land behind, with no intention of coming back
senses.definitionCN: 把房屋、城镇或土地丢下，并且不打算再回来
senses.example: The village was abandoned after the mine closed.
senses.exampleCN: 矿场关闭之后，这座村子被弃置了。
senses.why: The Old French phrase a bandon put something at another person's disposal; leaving a place for good is the strongest form of handing it over to nobody.
senses.whyCN: 古法语短语 a bandon 指把东西交给别人处置；永久离开一个地方，就是把交付对象变成了「没有人」。

senses.title: To desert someone who depends on you
senses.definition: to leave a person who relies on your care, especially a child or an animal
senses.definitionCN: 离开依赖你照顾的人，尤其是孩子或动物
senses.example: He was arrested for abandoning his dog on the motorway.
senses.exampleCN: 他因为把狗遗弃在高速公路上而被逮捕。
senses.why: The word keeps a legal tone: abandonment is a failure of duty, not merely a change of address.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了法律语气：遗弃是失职，而不只是换个住处。

senses.title: To give up a plan or effort
senses.definition: to stop working on a plan, project, or attempt before it is finished
senses.definitionCN: 在计划、项目或尝试完成之前停止做下去
senses.example: They abandoned the bridge project when the funding was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 资金被削减后，他们放弃了那座桥的项目。
senses.why: A project is held like an object in the hand; opening the hand is the physical gesture behind the figurative use.
senses.whyCN: 项目像手里的东西一样被握持；松开手，就是这一比喻用法背后的身体动作。

senses.title: To leave a ship in an emergency
senses.definition: to leave a ship, aircraft, or vehicle that is in danger, usually on orders
senses.definitionCN: 在船只、飞机或车辆遇险时离开，通常是奉命行事
senses.example: The order to abandon ship came when the deck began to flood.
senses.exampleCN: 甲板开始进水时，弃船的命令下来了。
senses.why: At sea, abandoning a vessel is a formal act with a fixed command, and the word keeps that emergency force.
senses.whyCN: 在海上，弃船是一个有固定口令的正式动作，这个词因此保留了那份紧急意味。

senses.title: To forsake a belief or principle
senses.definition: to stop upholding a belief, promise, or principle that one once held
senses.definitionCN: 不再坚持曾经持有的信念、承诺或原则
senses.example: The party abandoned its promise to protect the wetlands.
senses.exampleCN: 这个政党背弃了保护湿地的承诺。
senses.why: Values are treated as things one carries; dropping them is pictured as leaving them by the roadside.
senses.whyCN: 价值被当作随身携带的东西；把它们丢下，就像扔在路边。

senses.title: To give oneself up to a feeling
senses.definition: to let a feeling such as grief or joy take complete control of you
senses.definitionCN: 让悲伤、喜悦等情感完全控制自己
senses.example: She abandoned herself to grief after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，她任由悲伤淹没自己。
senses.why: Here the person is the thing left behind: control is abandoned, and the emotion takes the empty seat.
senses.whyCN: 这里被丢下的是人自己：控制被放弃，情感便坐上了空出来的位子。

intro.en: Abandon came into English from a French phrase, not from a Latin prefix, and its core idea is handing something over to another power.
intro.cn: abandon 是从一个法语短语进入英语的，而不是由拉丁前缀拼成；它的内核是把东西交给另一种支配力量。

items.en: Since the nineteenth century the phrase with abandon has meant unrestrained behaviour, while the verb kept its moral and legal force in reports of neglect.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，短语 with abandon 表示不加约束的举止；而动词在关于失职的报道中保留了道德与法律的分量。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century, at first in the sense of giving something over to another person's control.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个动词，最初表示把某物交给他人掌控。

items.en: Abandoner meant to hand over, surrender, or leave at someone's mercy, and it was used widely in legal writing.
items.cn: abandoner 意为交出、放弃或听凭他人处置，在法律文书中用得很多。

items.en: The verb grew out of the phrase a bandon, literally at disposal or under someone's jurisdiction.
items.cn: 这个动词由短语 a bandon 生长出来，字面意思是「听凭处置」或「在某人管辖之下」。

items.en: Bannum, from Frankish ban meaning a proclamation or command, gave the phrase its sense of authority over a person or thing.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 bannum 源自法兰克语 ban，意为公告或命令，正是它让这个短语带上了对人、对物的支配权。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms and near relatives of the same word; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for leaving people or things behind.
note.cn: 形近组收同一个词的各种形式与近亲；近义组收表示把人和物丢下的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act or state of being left behind.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「遗弃、弃置」，指被丢下的行为或状态。

entries.definition: Left empty and unused, or left without care.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「废弃的、被遗弃的」。

entries.definition: Software that its maker no longer supports or sells.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「弃置软件」，指开发者不再维护或销售的软件。

entries.definition: An official order forbidding something; it comes from the same proclamation word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「禁令、禁止」，出自同一个表示「公告」的词。

entries.definition: To leave a person or post without permission, especially in a duty-bound situation.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、擅离」，多指抛弃应负责的人或岗位。

entries.definition: To give up someone or something once valued, often in older or literary style.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「抛弃、背离」，语气文雅或偏古，多指舍弃曾珍视的人或物。

entries.definition: To let go of power, control, or a claim, often unwillingly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「放弃、交出」，常带不情愿的意味。

entries.definition: To get rid of something or leave someone abruptly, in casual speech.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「甩掉、丢下」，属口语说法。

entries.definition: To leave someone helpless in a place with no way to leave.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使滞留、使困在」，指让人无处可去。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real French parts of the word and the phrases it actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词真实的法语构件，以及它实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Break it as a plus band plus on: a band left the stage on and never came back.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 a 加 band 加 on：一支乐队上场后离开，再没回来。

normal.en: The Old French phrase a bandon meant at someone's disposal, so to abandon is to stop holding on.
normal.cn: 古法语短语 a bandon 意为听凭处置，所以 abandon 就是不再握持。

normal.en: Abandonment is the act and abandoned is the state; both grow straight from the verb.
normal.cn: abandonment 是行为，abandoned 是状态，两者都直接由这个动词生长出来。

normal.en: The fixed phrase abandon ship belongs to the emergency sense and appears in every account of a sinking.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 abandon ship 属于紧急义，凡记录沉船的文字里都会出现。

normal.en: With abandon reverses the feeling: control is gone, yet here the loss feels like freedom.
normal.cn: with abandon 把感受倒了过来：控制没有了，但在这里失去反而像自由。

abstract.en: Picture a lit room with the door open and the key left on the table: the person is gone, the place remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一间还亮着灯的房间，门开着，钥匙留在桌上：人走了，地方还在。

abstract.en: The same picture works for a promise dropped on the road, still readable in the dust.
abstract.cn: 同一个画面也适用于丢在路上的承诺，字迹还在尘土里。

abstract.en: Every sense turns on one gesture: the hand opens and whatever it held is no longer held.
abstract.cn: 所有义项都绕着一个动作：手张开，原先握着的就不再有握持。

examples.en: The crew had to abandon the sinking ship.
examples.cn: 船员们不得不弃船。

examples.en: She abandoned her plan to study abroad after her father fell ill.
examples.cn: 父亲病倒后，她放弃了出国留学的计划。

examples.en: They danced with abandon at the wedding.
examples.cn: 他们在婚礼上尽情起舞。

root: 古法语 abandoner「交出、放弃」← 短语 a bandon「听凭他人处置」，其中 ban 表「公告、管辖」；中世纪拉丁语 bannum 源自法兰克语 ban「宣告、命令」。十四世纪进入英语，先指「交出、听任」，后发展出「遗弃」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses all show one motion, release: a place, a person, a plan, a ship, a belief, and finally the self.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都指向同一个动作「松开」：松开一个地方、一个人、一份计划、一艘船、一种信念，最后是松开自己。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand opens and lets go of what it was holding.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手张开，放掉了原本握着的东物。

branches.en: THE PLACE AND THE PERSON: leaving a place and leaving a person are the same motion.
branches.cn: 地方与人线：离开一个地方与离开一个人，是同一个动作。

branches.en: THE PLAN: what was held in the hand is simply let go.
branches.cn: 计划线：手里握着的方案被松开。

branches.en: THE SHIP: at sea the gesture becomes a formal order.
branches.cn: 弃船线：在海上，这个动作变成正式口令。

branches.en: THE BELIEF: values can be dropped like luggage.
branches.cn: 信念线：价值观也能像行李一样被丢下。

branches.en: THE SELF: when control is surrendered, feeling takes the empty seat.
branches.cn: 自我线：交出控制后，情感坐上空出来的位子。

intro.en: The word is a French phrase turned into an English verb, so its parts are words rather than prefixes and suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是由一个法语短语变成的英语动词，因此它的构件是词而不是前后缀。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin abandonare and bannum are recorded; the deeper Frankish ban is reconstructed from historical evidence.

definition_zh: 有能力的；能干的；能够的；有才干的；有资格的

core_image: 一个人挽起袖子，手里握着能办成事的工具

pos.zh: 形容词：有能力的；能干的；能够的

senses.title: Having the power to do something
senses.definition: having enough skill, strength or chance to do a particular thing
senses.definitionCN: 具备足够的技能、力量或机会去做某件具体的事
senses.example: She was able to fix the old clock in under an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她不到一小时就修好了那座旧钟。
senses.why: Latin habilis meant easy to hold or handle, and an able person is one who can get a handle on the task.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 habilis 意为「容易握持、顺手」，能干的人就是能把任务握在手里的人。

senses.title: Skilful at work
senses.definition: showing real skill and effectiveness in a role or job
senses.definitionCN: 在某个岗位或工作中表现出真正的技能与成效
senses.example: He is an able manager who listens before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位先听后决的能干经理。
senses.why: The adjective moved from a single act to a whole reputation: able now describes the person, not only the deed.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从单个行为转到整体声誉：able 现在描述人，而不只是描述行为。

senses.title: Sound in body
senses.definition: in able-bodied, physically fit and free of disability
senses.definitionCN: 在 able-bodied 中，指身体健全、没有残障
senses.example: The race was open to able-bodied runners and wheelchair users.
senses.exampleCN: 这场比赛对健全跑者与轮椅使用者同样开放。
senses.why: Capability has a physical floor, and the compound names the body that meets it.
senses.whyCN: 能力有一个身体的下限，这个复合词指的就是达到这个下限的身体。

senses.title: Qualified in law
senses.definition: having the legal right or standing to do something
senses.definitionCN: 拥有做某事所需的法律权利或身份
senses.example: She is legally able to sign for the company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在法律上有资格代表公司签字。
senses.why: Capability is not only muscle but permission, and the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 能力不只是肌肉，也是许可，而这个词同时覆盖两者。

senses.title: Having the means
senses.definition: having enough money or resources to do something
senses.definitionCN: 拥有足够的钱或资源去做某事
senses.example: They were able to buy the house without a loan.
senses.exampleCN: 他们不用贷款就买下了那栋房子。
senses.why: A task can be blocked by cost as easily as by strength, so able extends to the means of doing.
senses.whyCN: 任务可以被成本挡住，就像可以被力气挡住，因此 able 也扩展到「做事的办法」。

intro.en: Able comes from a Latin word meaning handy. English moved it from things that fit to people who can act.
intro.cn: able 来自一个意为「顺手、好用」的拉丁词。英语把它从「合适的物」移到了「能行动的人」。

items.en: Be able to is now the ordinary way to express possibility in English, and able also describes competent people.
items.cn: be able to 如今是英语中表达可能性的普通说法，able 也用来形容能干的人。

items.en: Able seaman became an official rank, and able-bodied entered law and insurance as a description of fitness.
items.cn: able seaman 成为正式等级，able-bodied 进入法律与保险，用来描述体格健全。

items.en: English took the word from French and used it for both fitness and skill.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语从法语借入这个词，同时用于「合适」与「技能」。

items.en: Habilis meant handy or easy to hold, formed from habere to hold.
items.cn: habilis 意为「顺手的、容易握持的」，由 habere「握持」构成。

items.en: Habere, to hold or have, also gives English habit and exhibit, so the root picture is a hand that can grip.
items.cn: habere 意为「握持、拥有」，还产生英语的 habit 与 exhibit，词根画面是一只能抓住东西的手。

note.cn: 形近组收「能力」词族及其否定形式；近义组收表示胜任的形容词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep able tied to a hand that can grip the task.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想把 able 与「能握住任务的手」连起来。

normal.en: Able looks like a + ble: a person with a handle on the work.
normal.cn: able 可看作 a 加 ble：一个人把工作握在了手里。

normal.en: Enable puts the ability in; disable takes it out.
normal.cn: enable 把能力放进去，disable 把能力拿走。

normal.en: Able-bodied describes the body able to carry its own weight.

normal.en: Legal ability is permission, not muscle.
normal.cn: 法律上的 able 是许可，而不是肌肉。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around a doorknob exactly the right size.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手正好握住一个大小合适的门把手。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps a fit between person and task: strength, skill, money, permission, mind.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留人与任务之间的「相合」：力气、技能、钱、许可、头脑。

abstract.en: The oldest sense is the quietest: this thing is fit for that use.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义最安静：这件东西适合那个用途。

examples.en: The crew included an able seaman on every watch.

root: 拉丁语 habere「握持」→ habilis「顺手的」→ 法语 able → 英语 able。核心是「握得住」：握得住任务就有能力，握得住岗位就能干，握得住身体就健全，握得住许可就有资格，握得住钱就有办法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move from bare capacity to reputation, body, legal permission and finally money and means.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从单纯的能力，走到评价、身体、法律许可，最后是钱财与办法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closes around a tool that fits it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手握住一件合手的工具。

branches.en: THE CAPACITY: the hand can hold the task.
branches.cn: 能力线：手能握住那件事。

branches.en: THE REPUTATION: one act becomes a judgement about the whole person.
branches.cn: 评价线：一次表现变成对整个人的判断。

branches.en: THE BODY: ability has a physical floor.

branches.en: THE PERMISSION: ability is also a right to act.
branches.cn: 许可线：能力也是一种行动的资格。

branches.en: THE MEANS: a task can be blocked by cost as much as by strength.
branches.cn: 资源线：拦住一件事的，可以是成本，也可以是力气。

intro.en: Able is a Latin adjective of holding, and English built a full family of nouns, verbs and negatives around it.
intro.cn: able 是一个拉丁语「握持」形容词，英语围绕它建起了名词、动词与否定形式的完整词族。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is habere, habilis and able.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 habere、habilis 与 able。

items.example: It also gives habit and exhibit.
items.exampleCN: 它还产生 habit 与 exhibit。

items.example: It is the source of able and ability.
items.exampleCN: 它是 able 与 ability 的来源。

items.example: It is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是整个词族的词基。

items.example: It forms ability.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 ability。

items.example: It forms ably.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 ably。

items.example: It forms enable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 enable。

items.example: It forms disable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 disable。

items.example: It forms unable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 unable。

definition_zh: 反常的；异常的；不正常的；畸形的
definition_en: different from what is usual, expected, or healthy, especially in a way that causes concern
core_image: 一排整齐的方砖里，被塞进了一块尺寸不对的砖
scene: 体检报告上有一项数值高得离谱，医生又让人重测了一次。The scan showed an abnormal growth on the left side of the lung.
sceneCN: 这里 abnormal 指医学检查中的异常（第 1 个义项：身体上的异常）；句意为扫描显示左肺有一处异常增生。

pos.zh: 反常的；异常的；不正常的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「异常地；反常地」
由形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「异常；畸形」

senses.title: Not normal in the body
senses.definition: of a body part, cell, or growth, differing from what is healthy or usual
senses.definitionCN: 指身体部位、细胞或增生与健康、常见状态不同
senses.example: The test found abnormal cells in the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 检测在样本中发现了异常细胞。
senses.why: The Latin root names a carpenter's square, the tool that tests whether a line is true; cells that fail the test are abnormal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根指木匠的曲尺，是用来检验线条是否端正的工具；通不过检验的细胞就是异常。

senses.title: Deviating from usual behaviour
senses.definition: of behaviour or mental state, far from what is typical for a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 指行为或心理状态远离一个人或群体的常见样子
senses.example: His abnormal silence worried his friends.
senses.exampleCN: 他反常的沉默让朋友们担心。
senses.why: Behaviour is measured against what a group treats as the norm, and the word marks the distance from that line.
senses.whyCN: 行为以群体当作常规的尺度来衡量，这个词标记的就是偏离那条线的距离。

senses.title: Outside the expected range
senses.definition: of a measurement or reading, lying outside the range that is considered safe or typical
senses.definitionCN: 指测量值或读数落在被认为安全、正常范围之外
senses.example: The sensor recorded an abnormal rise in temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 传感器记录到温度的异常上升。
senses.why: A scale has a normal band, and any reading off that band is described with the same word used for bodies.
senses.whyCN: 刻度上有一段正常区间，落在区间之外的读数，就用描述身体的那个词来说。

senses.title: Rare in nature
senses.definition: of a natural event, occurring far less often than usual or outside its normal pattern
senses.definitionCN: 指自然事件出现得远少于平常，或脱离其常见规律
senses.example: An abnormal tide wiped out the lower path.
senses.exampleCN: 一场反常的潮水冲毁了低处的小路。
senses.why: Nature has a rhythm, and an event that breaks the rhythm is called abnormal even when nothing is wrong with it.
senses.whyCN: 自然有节奏，打破节奏的事件即便本身无害，也被称为反常。

intro.en: Abnormal is a Latin phrase made into an English adjective: away from the rule, with the rule itself imagined as a carpenter's square.
intro.cn: abnormal 是把一个拉丁短语做成了英语形容词：离开规则，而规则本身被想象成木匠的曲尺。

items.en: Modern English uses the word for anything outside the normal range, from cells to weather, and the adverb abnormally is common in reports.
items.cn: 现代英语用它指任何超出正常范围的东西，从细胞到天气；副词 abnormally 在报告里很常见。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in English in the early nineteenth century, formed on the French model rather than inherited from Latin.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪初见于英语，是照法语样式构成，而不是直接从拉丁语继承。

items.en: French anormal, itself from Latin, supplied the pattern for the English word.
items.cn: 法语 anormal 本身来自拉丁语，为英语词提供了构词样式。

items.en: Latin abnormis meant irregular or departing from rule, built from ab- meaning away from and norma meaning rule.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abnormis 意为「不合规则、离开规则」，由表示「离开」的 ab- 与表示「规则」的 norma 构成。

items.en: Norma was a carpenter's square, the tool that keeps a line true, and it also gave English norm and normal.
items.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺，是用来让线条端正的工具，它还给英语带来了 norm 与 normal。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin rule; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for things outside the usual pattern.
note.cn: 形近组收建在拉丁语「规则」上的词；近义组收表示脱离常见样式的形容词。

entries.definition: Something that deviates from the standard, but built on a Greek root instead.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「异常事物」，但建在希腊词根上。

entries.definition: Deviating from the normal order, the adjective matching anomaly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「反常的」，与 anomaly 对应。

entries.definition: In a way that departs from the usual or healthy pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「异常地、反常地」。

entries.definition: The standard that a group treats as normal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「规范、常态」，指群体视为正常的标准。

entries.definition: Not common, but often neutral rather than worrying.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不寻常的」，语气常是中性的，不带担忧。

entries.definition: Not following the normal pattern in shape, time, or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不规则的」，形状、时间或行为不合常规。

entries.definition: Departing from what is normal or acceptable, often of behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「越轨的、异常的」，多用于行为。

entries.definition: Not representative of its type, a milder and more clinical word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「非典型的」，语气更轻、更偏临床。

entries.definition: Strange and unnatural in a way that shocks or amuses.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「怪异的」，带令人惊讶或觉得好笑的意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin parts of the word and the places where it appears in ordinary life.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词的拉丁构件，以及它在日常生活中出现的场合。

normal.en: ab- means away from and normal means according to rule, so abnormal is simply away from the rule.
normal.cn: ab- 表示「离开」，normal 表示「合乎规则」，所以 abnormal 就是离开规则。

normal.en: Norma was a carpenter's square, the tool that tests a right angle; abnormal is the line that will not square.
normal.cn: norma 是木匠的曲尺，用来检验直角；abnormal 就是那条怎么量都不正的线。

normal.en: Anomaly is the noun and anomalous the adjective of the same idea, both built on Greek rather than Latin.
normal.cn: anomaly 是名词，anomalous 是形容词，表达同一意念，但两者建在希腊语而不是拉丁语上。

normal.en: Hospitals use abnormal for test results, and the word there is neutral, not an insult.
normal.cn: 医院用 abnormal 说检查结果，那里的语气是中性的，并不是骂人。

normal.en: Abnormal psychology is the fixed course name for the study of behaviour far from usual patterns.
normal.cn: abnormal psychology 是固定课程名，研究远离常见模式的行为。

abstract.en: Picture a row of identical tiles with one tile of the wrong size pushed into the line.
abstract.cn: 想象一排一模一样的砖，其中被塞进了一块尺寸不对的砖。

abstract.en: The gap it makes is what the eye notices first, before it can say what is wrong.
abstract.cn: 眼睛最先注意到的是它挤出的缝隙，然后才说得出哪里不对。

abstract.en: The same misfit tile appears in a blood test, a storm, and a design that breaks the pattern.
abstract.cn: 同一块不合尺寸的砖，会出现在血液检查、风暴，以及打破样式的设计里。

examples.en: The doctor ordered more tests after the abnormal result.
examples.cn: 结果异常之后，医生安排了更多检查。

examples.en: Such abnormal rainfall has not been seen in this region for decades.
examples.cn: 这种反常的降雨在这个地区几十年未见。

examples.en: The report described the sudden change in policy as abnormal.
examples.cn: 报告称政策的突然变化不合常规。

root: 拉丁语 abnormis「不合规则」＝ ab-「离开」＋ norma「曲尺、规范」；norma 还是英语 norm 与 normal 的来源。英语形容词见于十九世纪初，受法语 anormal 影响而成。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses apply one ruler, the normal range, to a body, a behaviour, a reading and a season.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项用同一把尺子「正常范围」，去量身体、行为、读数和季节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one tile of the wrong size is pushed into a row of identical tiles.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块尺寸不对的砖被塞进一排整齐相同的砖里。

branches.en: THE BODY: a cell that fails the carpenter's square is marked abnormal.
branches.cn: 身体线：通不过曲尺检验的细胞就被标为异常。

branches.en: THE BEHAVIOUR: the group supplies the line that the person departs from.
branches.cn: 行为线：群体提供那条被人偏离的线。

branches.en: THE READING: a scale has a normal band, and values outside it take the same word.
branches.cn: 读数线：刻度上有一段正常区间，区间外的数值也用这个词。

branches.en: THE SEASON: nature keeps a rhythm, and weather that ignores it is called abnormal.
branches.cn: 季节线：自然自有节奏，无视节奏的天气就被称作反常。

branches.en: THE SHARED RULER: every sense is a distance measured from an expected line.
branches.cn: 共同线：每个义项都是偏离一条预期线之后量出的距离。

intro.en: The word is Latin from end to end, with only the adjective ending added in English.
intro.cn: 这个词从头到尾都是拉丁语，英语只加了形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma, abnormis and normalis are recorded, so the parts are historical rather than reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 norma、abnormis 与 normalis 都有文献记录，因此这些构件属于有史可查的形式。

items.example: It is the rule against which things are measured.
items.exampleCN: 它是用来衡量事物的那把尺。

items.example: It is the short English form of the Latin noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是那个拉丁名词的英语短形式。

items.example: It is the positive word that abnormal negates.
items.exampleCN: 它是 abnormal 所否定的正面词。

items.example: It is the Latin source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词的拉丁语来源。

items.example: It forms abnormal from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁词干构成 abnormal。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 abnormally。

items.example: It expresses the same idea from a Greek root.
items.exampleCN: 它从希腊词根表达同一意念。

definition_zh: 废除；废止；取消；撤销
definition_en: to end a law, system, practice, or institution officially and completely
core_image: 一张写满条款的纸被撕成两半，桌上的旧印章也被收走
scene: 议会大厅里最后一票投完，墙角那部旧法规的牌子被人摘了下来。The country voted to abolish the death penalty in the spring.
sceneCN: 这里 abolish 指正式废除一项法律（第 1 个义项：废除法律）；句意为这个国家在春天投票废除了死刑。

pos.zh: 废除；废止（法律、制度、习俗）
取消；撤销（机构、费用、限制）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ition 构成，义为「废除；废止」
由 abolition 加 -ist 构成，义为「废奴主义者；主张废除者」
由动词加表人后缀 -er 构成，义为「废除者」

senses.title: To end a law officially
senses.definition: to put an end to a law by an official act, so that it no longer has force
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式程序终止一项法律，使它不再有效力
senses.example: Parliament abolished the old licensing rules last year.
senses.exampleCN: 议会去年废除了那套旧的许可规定。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to destroy or blot out; a law that is abolished is erased from the statute book.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「摧毁、抹去」；被废除的法律，就是从法典上被擦掉。

senses.title: To end a system or practice
senses.definition: to stop a long-established system or custom from operating any further
senses.definitionCN: 让长期存在的制度或习俗不再继续运作
senses.example: The reform abolished the practice of paying for school places.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革废止了为学位付费的做法。
senses.why: A practice is held up by repetition; ending it means cutting the repetition at its root.
senses.whyCN: 惯例靠重复支撑；终止它，就是从根上切断重复。

senses.title: To close an institution
senses.definition: to do away with an office, department, or post as a permanent arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 永久取消某个机构、部门或职位
senses.example: The ministry abolished three regional offices in the same decree.
senses.exampleCN: 该部在同一道法令里撤销了三个地区办事处。
senses.why: An institution is a body with a place in the structure; abolishing it removes that place entirely.
senses.whyCN: 机构是在结构里占一个位置的实体；废除它就是把这个位置整个拿掉。

intro.en: Abolish comes from a Latin verb for wiping something out, and the metaphor of erasure still sits under every official use of the word.
intro.cn: abolish 来自一个意为「抹掉」的拉丁动词，抹除的比喻至今仍垫在这个词每一种正式用法的下面。

items.en: The word is now mostly used of laws, institutions, and practices, and abolition is the standard noun in political history.
items.cn: 现代这个词多用于法律、机构与惯例，而 abolition 是政治史里的标准名词。

items.en: English borrowed the verb through French in the fifteenth century, first in the sense of destroying or doing away with something.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪经法语借入这个动词，最初表示摧毁或除去某物。

items.en: Old French abolir meant to destroy or wipe out, and it carried the legal sense of repealing a custom.
items.cn: 古法语 abolir 意为摧毁或抹掉，并带有废止某项惯例的法律含义。

items.en: Abolere meant to destroy, efface, or blot out, and its past participle abolitus lies behind the English adjective and noun forms.
items.cn: abolere 意为摧毁、抹去、擦掉，其过去分词 abolitus 正是英语形容词与名词形式背后的形态。

items.en: The prefix ab- meaning away from marks removal, which is why the word always suggests something taken out of existence.
items.cn: 表示「离开」的前缀 ab- 标记移除，因此这个词总暗示某物被从存在中拿走。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same Latin verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for cancelling rules and institutions.
note.cn: 形近组收建在同一拉丁动词上的形式；近义组收表示取消规则与机构的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of ending a law, system, or institution.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废除、废止」，指终止法律、制度或机构的行为。

entries.definition: A person who campaigns for abolishing a practice, especially slavery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废奴主义者」，指主张废除某制度的人。

entries.definition: A rarer noun for the same act, built with -ment instead of -ition.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义同「废除」，是较罕见的 -ment 形式。

entries.definition: A person or thing that abolishes something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「废除者」，指废除某事物的人或物。

entries.definition: To end a law by the same authority that made it, the usual word in legislatures.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废止、撤销」，由立法机关撤销法律，是议会里的常用词。

entries.definition: To cancel a licence, right, or permission officially.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撤销、吊销」，用于执照、权利或许可。

entries.definition: To declare a marriage or agreement no longer valid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣布无效」，用于婚姻或协议。

entries.definition: To destroy something bad completely, especially a disease or a practice.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「根除」，指彻底消灭疾病或不良做法。

entries.definition: To remove something completely, often a risk or a difference.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「消除、排除」，多指风险或差别。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the erasing image inside the Latin root and the causes the word is usually attached to.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁词根里「擦掉」的形象，以及这个词常挂在哪些对象上。

normal.en: The Latin root meant to blot out, so abolishing a rule is rubbing the line off the page.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根意为「擦掉」，所以废除一条规则就是把那一行从纸页上擦去。

normal.en: Abolition is the act and abolitionist is the person who campaigns for it, both built straight on the verb.
normal.cn: abolition 是行为，abolitionist 是为此奔走的人，两者都直接建在动词上。

normal.en: The fixed phrase abolish the death penalty is the most public use of the word.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 abolish the death penalty 是这个词最公开的用法。

normal.en: Abolish a tax is the everyday use in budget news, and the charge simply disappears from the ledger.
normal.cn: abolish a tax 是预算新闻里的日常用法，那笔收费就从账本上消失。

normal.en: The word is final: what is abolished does not come back next year.
normal.cn: 这个词是终局性的：被废除的东西不会明年再回来。

abstract.en: Picture a sheet of clauses torn down the middle, the two halves no longer able to complete each other.
abstract.cn: 想象一张写满条款的纸从中间撕开，两半再也拼不成一句完整的话。

abstract.en: The old stamp is taken off the desk, and with it the authority to enforce anything.
abstract.cn: 旧印章被从桌上拿走，随之而去的还有执行任何规定的权力。

abstract.en: Erasing, tearing, and closing an office are one gesture: the thing is no longer there to be used.
abstract.cn: 擦掉、撕掉、关掉一个机构，是同一个动作：那件东西不再在那里可供使用。

examples.en: The government abolished the tax on imported medicine.
examples.cn: 政府取消了进口药品的税。

examples.en: Slavery was abolished in the colony in the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 这个殖民地在十九世纪废除了奴隶制。

examples.en: The committee voted to abolish the post of deputy director.
examples.cn: 委员会投票决定撤销副主任这一职位。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，不立世」——旧的法规不再立于世，被撕掉了

root: 拉丁语 abolere「摧毁、抹去」← ab-「离开」＋ 古词根 olere「生长、滋长」，字面带有「使停止生长」的意味；过去分词 abolitus。英语经古法语 abolir 借入，十五世纪已有记录。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses cover the removal of a law, of an institution or custom, and of an office itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项分别覆盖取消法律、废止制度或惯例，以及撤销机构本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clause on a page is struck through with a single line.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸页上的一条条文被一笔划掉。

branches.en: THE LAW: a statute struck from the book.
branches.cn: 法律线：从法典里划掉一条法令。

branches.en: THE CUSTOM: a practice that loses its force.
branches.cn: 惯例线：一种做法失去约束力。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: an institution or post ceases to exist.
branches.cn: 机构线：一个机构或职位不再存在。

branches.en: THE UNBINDING: what was binding is no longer binding.
branches.cn: 解缚线：原本有约束力的东西不再有约束力。

branches.en: THE ENDING: the thing itself is made not to exist.
branches.cn: 终止线：事物本身被弄得不再存在。

intro.en: The word is Latin and French in origin, and its parts still read as a prefix of removal plus a verb of growth.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语与法语，它的部件至今仍可读作「移除」前缀加「生长」动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin abolere and abolitus are recorded; the deeper root olere is archaic and only partly attested.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abolere 与 abolitus 有文献记录；更深的词根 olere 属古旧形式，只有部分可考。

items.example: The prefix marks removal from existence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记从存在中被移除。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It lies behind the noun abolition.
items.exampleCN: 它是名词 abolition 背后的形态。

items.example: French carried the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个词带进了英语。

items.example: It forms the English verb abolish.
items.exampleCN: 它构成英语动词 abolish。

items.example: It forms abolition.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abolition。

items.example: It forms abolitionist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abolitionist。

items.example: It forms abolisher.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abolisher。

由 abolition 加 -ist 构成，义为「废奴主义者；主张废除者」
由动词加表人后缀构成，义为「废除者」

definition_zh: 中止；使夭折；流产；放弃
definition_en: to stop a plan, process, or operation before it is finished, or to end a pregnancy early
core_image: 一枚刚点火的火箭在半空突然熄火，掉头落回地面
scene: 控制室里的倒计时走到一半，屏幕上跳出红色警告，工程师们把手从按钮上移开。The launch was aborted ten seconds before lift-off.
sceneCN: 这里 abort 指中止发射任务（第 2 个义项：中止技术操作）；句意为发射在升空前十秒被中止。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -tion 构成，义为「流产；堕胎；中途失败」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「夭折的；失败的」
由本词与拉丁词干合成，义为「堕胎药」，也可作形容词

senses.title: To stop a plan before it is finished
senses.definition: to end a plan or project deliberately while it is still under way
senses.definitionCN: 在计划或项目仍在进行时有意将其终止
senses.example: The company aborted the expansion after the first survey.
senses.exampleCN: 第一轮调研之后，公司中止了扩张计划。
senses.why: The Latin verb described a birth that stops before its time, and a plan can stop before its time in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词描述未足月就停止的分娩，计划也可以同样未到时辰就停住。

senses.title: To cancel a launch or operation
senses.definition: to stop a launch, flight, or technical operation before or during its start
senses.definitionCN: 在发射、飞行或技术操作开始前或开始过程中将其停止
senses.example: The launch was aborted ten seconds before lift-off.
senses.exampleCN: 发射在升空前十秒被中止。
senses.why: Mission control needs one word that means everything stops now, and this is that word.
senses.whyCN: 任务控制需要一个词表示「现在就全部停下」，用的正是这个词。

senses.title: To end a pregnancy deliberately
senses.definition: in medicine, to end a pregnancy by a medical procedure
senses.definitionCN: 在医学上，通过医疗手段终止妊娠
senses.example: The clinic provides counselling before a patient decides to abort.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所会在病人决定终止妊娠之前提供咨询。
senses.why: The medical sense is the oldest surviving one, and it keeps the plain meaning of a process stopped early.
senses.whyCN: 医学义是留存下来的最古老含义，它保留了「过程提前停止」这一朴素意义。

senses.title: To miscarry naturally
senses.definition: of a pregnancy, to end on its own before the fetus can survive
senses.definitionCN: 指妊娠在胎儿能够存活之前自行结束
senses.example: The ewe aborted in the cold snap and had to be watched closely.
senses.exampleCN: 寒潮中那只母羊流产了，得密切观察。
senses.why: Before it named an operation, the word simply reported that a pregnancy had not reached its term.
senses.whyCN: 在指手术之前，这个词只是报告一次妊娠没有到足月。

intro.en: Abort began as a word about a birth that never reached its term, and every later sense is a process stopped before its proper end.
intro.cn: abort 最初说的是没有到足月的生产，之后每一个义项都是「在应有的终点之前停住的过程」。

items.en: Modern use extends from medicine to computing and spaceflight, always with the sense of a deliberate stop.
items.cn: 现代用法从医学延伸到计算机与航天，始终带有「有意停止」的意味。

items.en: English took the verb from Latin in the sixteenth century, first in the medical sense of a pregnancy ending early.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语借入这个动词，最初用于妊娠提前结束的医学义。

items.en: Abortus was the noun for a miscarriage, and abortiri was the deponent verb meaning to miscarry or fail.
items.cn: abortus 是表示流产的名词，abortiri 则是意为「流产、失败」的异态动词。

items.en: The verb was built from ab- meaning away and oriri meaning to rise or be born, so it pictured a rising that never happened.
items.cn: 这个动词由表示「离开」的 ab- 与表示「升起、出生」的 oriri 构成，画面是一次没有发生的升起。

items.en: Oriri also gave English orient and origin, both naming a beginning or a rising point.
items.cn: oriri 还给英语带来了 orient 与 origin，两者都指开端或升起的起点。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for stopping something that has already begun.
note.cn: 形近组收建在同一词根上的形式；近义组收表示停止已开始之事的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an early end to a pregnancy, or a plan that failed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「流产、堕胎」，也指中途失败的计划。

entries.definition: Failing to produce the intended result, as in an abortive attempt.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「夭折的、失败的」，如 abortive attempt。

entries.definition: A drug or substance that causes a pregnancy to end.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「堕胎药」，也可作形容词指「引起流产的」。

entries.definition: Stopped before completion, as in an aborted launch.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「中止的、未完成的」，如 aborted launch。

entries.definition: To decide that a planned event or order will not happen at all.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「取消」，指决定原定的事不发生。

entries.definition: To cancel an event or an operation, often at short notice.
entries.definitionCN: 短语动词，义为「取消」，常在临近时叫停。

entries.definition: To bring something to an end, especially a contract or a process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「终止」，多用于合同或进程。

entries.definition: To lose a pregnancy naturally before the fetus can survive.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「自然流产」，指胎儿未能存活前妊娠自行结束。

entries.definition: To abandon a plan or project completely, in informal use.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「废弃、放弃」，口语中指彻底丢开计划。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the birth image inside the Latin root and the technical settings where the word now appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁词根里「出生」的形象，以及这个词今天出现的各种技术场景。

normal.en: The Latin parts are ab- meaning away and oriri meaning to rise, so abort is a rising that is called off.
normal.cn: 拉丁构件是表示「离开」的 ab- 与表示「升起」的 oriri，所以 abort 是一次被叫停的升起。

normal.en: Origin and orient come from the same oriri, all three words about a beginning or a rising point.
normal.cn: origin 与 orient 出自同一个 oriri，三个词都关于开端或升起的起点。

normal.en: In mission control the single word abort means everything stops now.
normal.cn: 在任务控制里，单个词 abort 意思是「现在全部停下」。

normal.en: A computer aborts a process the way a rocket aborts a launch: before the planned end.
normal.cn: 计算机中止进程，就像火箭中止发射：都在预定的终点之前停住。

normal.en: Abortive describes the attempt that failed, and aborted describes the thing that was stopped.
normal.cn: abortive 描述失败了的尝试，aborted 描述被中止了的事物。

abstract.en: Picture a countdown frozen at the last second, the engine lit but the rocket still on the pad.
abstract.cn: 想象倒计时停在最后一秒，引擎已经点火，火箭却仍留在发射台上。

abstract.en: The same frozen countdown appears in an operating theatre and in a program waiting for a signal.
abstract.cn: 同一个被冻住的倒计时，也出现在手术室和等待信号的程序里。

abstract.en: Every use is a flight cut short, and the word is about the cut, not about the crash.
abstract.cn: 每一次用法都是一次被截短的飞行，这个词讲的是那一刀，而不是坠毁。

examples.en: The crew aborted the mission when the fuel reading fell.
examples.cn: 燃料读数下降时，机组中止了任务。

examples.en: The software will abort the download if the file is corrupted.
examples.cn: 如果文件损坏，软件会中止下载。

examples.en: They aborted the trial after the first results were clearly negative.
examples.cn: 首批结果明显为负面后，他们中止了试验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊，波特」——波特在倒计时最后一秒按下停止，火箭没有起飞

root: 拉丁语 abortiri「流产、失败」← ab-「离开」＋ oriri「升起、出生」，字面即「未能升起」；名词 abortus 指流产。同根还产生 origin 与 orient。英语十六世纪借入，先为医学义，后扩展到任务与计算机。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses stop three kinds of process early: a plan, a launch or operation, a pregnancy, and a natural pregnancy loss.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项分别提前叫停计划、发射或操作、妊娠，以及自然发生的流产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a countdown stops at the last second and the rocket never rises.
core.cn: 核心意象：倒计时停在最后一秒，火箭始终没有升起。

branches.en: THE PLAN: something is called off before it matures.
branches.cn: 计划线：事情还没成熟就被叫停。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: a launch or procedure is cut off midway.
branches.cn: 操作线：发射或程序在中途被切断。

branches.en: THE PREGNANCY: the medical ending of a pregnancy.
branches.cn: 医学线：在医学上终止妊娠。

branches.en: THE NATURAL LOSS: the body ends a pregnancy without help.
branches.cn: 自然线：身体在没有外力介入时终止妊娠。

branches.en: THE EARLY STOP: every sense is a halt before completion.
branches.cn: 中止线：每个义项都是在完成之前停住。

intro.en: The word is Latin plus a plain English verb ending, and the two Latin parts still explain every sense.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语加一个普通英语动词词尾，两个拉丁部件至今能解释每一个义项。

latinIntro.en: Latin abortus, abortiri, and oriri are recorded, so no part of the word needs reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abortus、abortiri 与 oriri 都有文献记录，这个词没有任何部件需要重构。

items.exampleCN: 它标记那一次没有发生的升起。

items.example: It also gives origin and orient.
items.exampleCN: 它还产生了 origin 与 orient。

items.example: It is the Latin verb behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语词背后的拉丁动词。

items.example: It is the noun that gave abortion.
items.exampleCN: 它正是产生 abortion 的名词。

items.example: It entered English in the sixteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 它在十六世纪进入英语。

items.example: It forms abortion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortion。

items.example: It forms abortive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortive。

items.example: It forms abortifacient.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortifacient。

由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「夭折的；失败的」
由本词与拉丁词干合成，义为「堕胎药」

definition_zh: 流产；堕胎；人工流产手术；中途失败
definition_en: the ending of a pregnancy before the fetus can survive, either naturally or by medical procedure
core_image: 一颗还没长成的种子，在半途停住了生长
scene: 诊所走廊上排着一列长椅，墙上贴着术前须知的告示。The law allowed abortion only where the mother's life was at risk.
sceneCN: 这里 abortion 指法律语境下的人工流产（第 1 个义项：人工流产）；句意为法律只在母亲生命受威胁时才允许人工流产。

pos.zh: （计划的）中途失败；夭折的事物

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「中止；流产」
由本词词干加 -ive 构成，义为「夭折的；失败的」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「施行堕胎者」，今多含贬义

senses.title: A medical termination of pregnancy
senses.definition: the deliberate ending of a pregnancy by a medical procedure
senses.definitionCN: 通过医疗手段有意终止妊娠
senses.example: The law allowed abortion only where the mother's life was at risk.
senses.exampleCN: 法律只在母亲生命受威胁时才允许人工流产。
senses.why: The Latin noun simply meant a birth cut short, and medicine kept that plain description without adding judgement.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词本义就是「被截短的生产」，医学沿用了这一朴素描述，不附加评判。

senses.title: A natural loss of pregnancy
senses.definition: the ending of a pregnancy by itself, before the fetus can survive
senses.definitionCN: 妊娠在胎儿能够存活之前自行结束
senses.example: The report recorded a spontaneous abortion in the third month.
senses.exampleCN: 报告记录了第三个月的自然流产。
senses.why: In clinical writing spontaneous abortion is the neutral term for what everyday speech calls a miscarriage.
senses.whyCN: 在临床文字里，spontaneous abortion 是日常所说 miscarriage 的中性术语。

senses.title: The procedure itself
senses.definition: the operation or treatment by which a pregnancy is ended
senses.definitionCN: 用来终止妊娠的手术或治疗过程
senses.example: The clinic explained the risks of the abortion in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所详细说明了这台流产手术的风险。
senses.why: A noun ending in -tion can name either the event or the procedure that produces it, and here it is the procedure.
senses.whyCN: 以 -tion 结尾的名词既能指事件，也能指产生该事件的手术，这里指的是手术。

intro.en: Abortion is the noun of a birth that does not reach its term, and the word has been medical, legal, and figurative in turn.
intro.cn: abortion 是「没有到足月的生产」的名词，这个词先后在医学、法律与比喻三个领域使用。

items.en: Modern English splits the sense between the medical event, the legal right, and a contemptuous word for a failed project.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词分成医学事件、法定权利，以及对失败计划的轻蔑说法。

items.en: The noun entered English in the sixteenth century through Latin, at first as a medical term for an early end to pregnancy.
items.cn: 这个名词在十六世纪经拉丁语进入英语，最初是妊娠提前结束的医学术语。

items.en: Abortio named a miscarriage, formed from abortus, the noun for the same event.
items.cn: abortio 指流产，由表示同一事件的名词 abortus 构成。

items.en: Abortus came from abortiri, to miscarry, which joined ab- meaning away with oriri meaning to be born.
items.cn: abortus 出自 abortiri「流产」，后者把表示「离开」的 ab- 与表示「出生」的 oriri 结合起来。

items.en: The same oriri, to rise or be born, lies behind origin and orient, so the word's family is all about beginnings.
items.cn: 同一个 oriri 意为「升起、出生」，也是 origin 与 orient 的来源，因此这一族词都与开端有关。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same birth root; the near-meaning group gathers medical and general terms for an early end.
note.cn: 形近组收出自同一「出生」词根的词；近义组收表示提前结束的医学与一般说法。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to stop a process or a pregnancy before its end.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「中止、流产」，指过程或妊娠提前结束。

entries.definition: Failing completely, as in an abortive attempt to negotiate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「夭折的、失败的」，如 abortive attempt to negotiate。

entries.definition: A substance that brings a pregnancy to an end.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「堕胎药」，指引起妊娠终止的药物。

entries.definition: The medical Latin term for a fetus lost before it could survive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，医学拉丁语中指未能存活即被排出的胎儿。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a pregnancy lost naturally, without a procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「自然流产」，是日常说法，不涉及手术。

entries.definition: A neutral clinical word for ending a pregnancy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「终止妊娠」，是临床上的中性说法。

entries.definition: A complete and humiliating failure of a plan or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「惨败」，指计划或表现的彻底失败。

entries.definition: A lack of success in doing or achieving something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「失败」，指未能做成或达成某事。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the birth image in the Latin root and the settings where the word is used today.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用拉丁词根里的「出生」形象，以及这个词今天使用的场合。

normal.en: The root oriri means to rise or be born, so an abortion is a rising that stops before it reaches the light.
normal.cn: 词根 oriri 意为「升起、出生」，所以 abortion 是一次还没见到天光就停住的升起。

normal.en: Spontaneous abortion is the clinical name for a miscarriage; the words differ in tone, not in event.
normal.cn: spontaneous abortion 是自然流产的临床名称，两种说法语气不同，事件相同。

normal.en: The -tion ending makes the noun cover both the event and the procedure.
normal.cn: -tion 后缀让这个名词同时覆盖事件与手术过程。

normal.en: The figurative use, an abortion of a plan, keeps the same picture of something that never came to term.
normal.cn: 比喻用法 an abortion of a plan 保留着同一幅画面：某物从未足月。

normal.en: In law the word shifts again, naming a right rather than an event.
normal.cn: 在法律里这个词再次转移，指的是权利而不是事件。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that stops growing while it is still small, the soil around it unchanged.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗种子还很小就停止生长，周围的土壤没有任何变化。

abstract.en: The same stopped growth can be seen in a building left half-built, which is how the contemptuous sense works.
abstract.cn: 同样的停止生长也可以在一座只建了一半的楼上看到，轻蔑义就是这么来的。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps one point: the end comes before the natural end.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都守住同一点：结束发生在自然的终点之前。

examples.en: The clinic offers counselling before and after an abortion.
examples.cn: 诊所在流产前后都提供咨询。

examples.en: The study compared abortion rates across three countries.
examples.cn: 这项研究比较了三个国家的流产率。

examples.en: The whole project was an abortion that wasted two years.
examples.cn: 整个项目是个夭折的烂摊子，浪费了两年时间。

root: 拉丁语 abortio「流产」← abortus ← abortiri「流产、失败」＝ ab-「离开」＋ oriri「升起、出生」；同根还有 origin 与 orient。英语十六世纪经拉丁语借入，先为医学术语，后扩展出法律与比喻用法。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses name the deliberate ending of a pregnancy, the natural loss of one, and the operation itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项分别指人为终止妊娠、自然流产，以及那台手术本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed stops growing while it is still small.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗种子还很小的时候停止了生长。

branches.en: THE DELIBERATE ENDING: a pregnancy is stopped on purpose.
branches.cn: 人为终止线：妊娠被有意终止。

branches.en: THE NATURAL LOSS: the same noun covers a loss that happens by itself.
branches.cn: 自然流失线：同一个名词也指自行发生的流失。

branches.en: THE OPERATION: the procedure is named by its outcome.
branches.cn: 手术线：那台手术以它的结果命名。

branches.en: THE MEDICAL FIELD: both belong to obstetrics, told apart by intention.
branches.cn: 医学线：两者同属产科，靠是否出于意愿来区分。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: the noun serves both for the event and for the visit.
branches.cn: 临床线：这个名词既指事件，也指那次就诊。

intro.en: The word is Latin through and through, and the two parts of its root explain the whole family.
intro.cn: 这个词彻头彻尾是拉丁语，词根的两个部件解释了整族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin abortio, abortus, and oriri are recorded, so only the English noun ending is a later addition.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 abortio、abortus 与 oriri 都有文献记录，只有英语名词词尾是后来加上的。

items.example: It marks the birth that does not arrive.
items.exampleCN: 它标记那一次没有到来的出生。

items.example: It is also the root of origin.
items.exampleCN: 它也是 origin 的词根。

items.example: It is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是名词背后的动词。

items.example: It is the base of abortio.
items.exampleCN: 它是 abortio 的词基。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语名词的直接来源。

items.example: It forms abortion from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 它由拉丁词干构成 abortion。

items.example: It forms abortive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortive。

items.example: It forms abortionist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abortionist。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉名词后缀构成，义为「中止；流产」
由本词词干加 -ive 构成，义为「夭折的；失败的」
由本词加 -ist 构成，义为「施行堕胎者」，今多含贬义

definition_zh: 关于；大约；在附近；四处；将近；即将；忙于；转向
definition_en: on the subject of something, approximately, nearby, in various directions, or on the point of doing something
core_image: 一个人绕着某个中心打转，既贴着它，又说不准精确位置
scene: 雨还没停，站台上的人已经把行李挪到脚边。The train is about to leave, so hurry up.
sceneCN: 这里 about 与 to 连用，表示「即将」（第 6 个义项：即将动身）；句意为火车就要开了，请快点。

derivatives.zh: 由 about 与 face 合成，义为「态度或方向的彻底转变」
由 round 与 about 合成，义为「环岛；迂回的说法」
由 there 与 about 合成，义为「大约在那附近」
由 here 与 about 合成，义为「在这一带」

senses.title: Concerning a subject
senses.definition: on the subject of something, or connected with it
senses.definitionCN: 涉及某个主题，或与它相关
senses.example: The lecture was about the origins of language.
senses.exampleCN: 这场讲座讲的是语言的起源。
senses.why: The oldest sense is around or on the outside, and speech about a thing circles the thing without touching its centre.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是「在周围、在外侧」；谈论一件事，就是绕着它说而不直达中心。

senses.title: Approximately
senses.definition: a little more or less than a stated number or amount
senses.definitionCN: 比所说的数目或数量略多或略少
senses.example: The journey takes about three hours.
senses.exampleCN: 这段旅程大约需要三个小时。
senses.why: From around comes roughly around a figure: the number is a centre, and the true value sits near it.
senses.whyCN: 由「在周围」引申出「大致在某个数字附近」：数字是中心，真实值就在它附近。

senses.title: Nearby or around a place
senses.definition: in or to various places near a point, or moving through an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某处附近，或在某一区域内移动
senses.example: They wandered about the market until dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在市场里逛到天黑。
senses.why: The spatial core of the word is simply the space surrounding an object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的空间内核，就是围绕某个物体的那片范围。

senses.title: In circulation or present somewhere
senses.definition: present in a place, often in an unspecified or widespread way
senses.definitionCN: 存在于某地，常指说不清具体位置或范围较广
senses.example: There is a lot of flu about this winter.
senses.exampleCN: 今年冬天流行性感冒很多。
senses.why: Illness that is about is illness moving around the population rather than sitting in one body.
senses.whyCN: 所谓四处「在」的病，是在人群里流动，而不是待在一具身体里。

senses.title: Busy with something
senses.definition: occupied with an activity, in older or literary usage
senses.definitionCN: 忙于某项活动，属较旧或偏文雅的用法
senses.example: What are you about so early in the morning?
senses.exampleCN: 你一大早忙什么呢？
senses.why: To be about a task is to be moving around inside it, the way one moves about a room.
senses.whyCN: 忙于一件事，就是在其中来回动作，如同在房间里走动。

senses.title: On the point of doing something
senses.definition: ready to do something almost immediately
senses.definitionCN: 几乎立刻就要做某事
senses.example: The meeting is about to begin.
senses.exampleCN: 会议即将开始。
senses.why: The sense grew from around the corner: the action is so near that one is already circling it.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项由「就在转角处」发展而来：动作近得人已经在它周围打转。

intro.en: About is a native English word built from a preposition and a word for the outside, and its history runs from space to topic.
intro.cn: about 是英语本族词，由一个介词和一个表示「外侧」的词构成，它的历史从空间一路走到话题。

items.en: Since the seventeenth century the word has covered approximate numbers and topics as easily as places.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，这个词既能指大致数目和话题，也能指地点，用起来一样自然。

items.en: By the sixteenth century about was common in the phrase about to, marking an action on the edge of happening.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，about 已常见于短语 about to，表示一个动作正处在发生的边缘。

items.en: Middle English abouten extended the old word to mean around, concerning, and approximately.
items.cn: 中古英语 abouten 把这个旧词扩展到「围绕、关于、大约」等意思。

items.en: The Old English form combined on, meaning in or on, with būtan, meaning outside or around.
items.cn: 古英语形式把表示「在……上」的 on 与表示「在外、在周围」的 būtan 组合起来。

items.en: Both parts go back to Germanic stock: the second element is related to English but, which originally meant outside.
items.cn: 两部分都可追溯到日耳曼语：后一构件与英语的 but 同源，本义是「在外侧」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and near forms built on about; the near-meaning group collects words for approximation and surrounding.
note.cn: 形近组收由 about 构成的复合词与近形；近义组收表示「大约」和「围绕」的词。

entries.definition: A complete reversal of direction, attitude, or policy.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「彻底转向；态度大转弯」。

entries.definition: A circular junction, or an indirect way of speaking.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，义为「环岛；迂回的」。

entries.definition: Near that place or roughly that number.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在那附近；大约那个数目」。

entries.definition: In this neighbourhood or area.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在这一带」。

entries.definition: Close to a stated figure but not exactly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「大约、近似地」。

entries.definition: On every side of something, or in a circle.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……周围；到处」。

entries.definition: Approximately, without exact detail.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「粗略地、大约」。

entries.definition: On the subject of; a formal equivalent of about.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「关于」，语气正式。

entries.definition: Almost, but not quite.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「几乎、将近」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real parts of the word and the phrases it actually keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用这个词真实的构件，以及它实际保留的搭配。

normal.en: Split it as a plus bout: a bout is a short round, and something about to happen is one round away.
normal.cn: 拆成 a 加 bout：bout 是一个短回合，即将发生的事只差一个回合。

normal.en: The second half once meant outside, so about places you on the outside of a thing, looking around it.
normal.cn: 词的后半过去表示「在外」，所以 about 把你放在一件事的外侧，绕着它看。

normal.en: About to is a fixed warning: the train about to leave is already moving in your mind.
normal.cn: about to 是固定的预警：即将开出的火车，在你心里已经动了。

normal.en: Compounds keep the same picture: a roundabout sends traffic in a circle, an about-face turns you right round.
normal.cn: 复合词沿用同一画面：环岛让车流绕圈，about-face 让人整个转过来。

normal.en: Learn it with its partners: about half, about time, all about, what about.
normal.cn: 连着伙伴一起记：about half、about time、all about、what about。

abstract.en: Think of a dot with a circle drawn around it: about never lands on the dot, it only circles.
abstract.cn: 想象一个点，外面画一个圈：about 从不落在点上，只是绕着转。

abstract.en: That circle is why one word can mean nearby, approximately, and concerning: each is a way of staying around the centre.
abstract.cn: 正是这个圈让一个词同时表示附近、大约和关于：三者都是待在中心周围的方式。

abstract.en: When the circle tightens to nothing, about becomes about to: the action is no longer near, it is next.
abstract.cn: 当圈子收紧到没有，about 就变成 about to：动作不再只是靠近，而是下一步。

examples.en: She told us a story about her grandmother.
examples.cn: 她给我们讲了一个关于她祖母的故事。

examples.en: The repair will cost about two hundred pounds.
examples.cn: 这次修理大约要花两百英镑。

examples.en: The children were running about in the garden.
examples.cn: 孩子们在花园里到处跑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿包特」——阿包特绕着摊位转了三圈，问遍了所有摊主

root: 古英语 onbūtan ← on「在……上」+ būtan「在外侧」，与英语 but 同源；中古英语作 abouten，义为「围绕、关于、大约」，十六世纪起 about to 表「即将」。词义从空间上的「绕在周围」引申到话题上的「关于」与数量上的「大约」。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses circle a topic, a quantity, a neighbourhood, scattered movement, occupation and near arrival.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项围绕一个话题、一个数量、一片附近、四散的移动、手头的事务和即将发生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a point with a circle drawn around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个点，外面画着一个圈。

branches.en: THE TOPIC: speech turns around a subject.
branches.cn: 主题线：话语绕着某个题目转。

branches.en: THE AMOUNT: a number is approached but not fixed.
branches.cn: 数量线：接近某个数目，却不钉死。

branches.en: THE NEIGHBOURHOOD: position near a place.
branches.cn: 近处线：在某个地方附近。

branches.en: THE SCATTER: movement or presence in all directions.
branches.cn: 四散线：朝各个方向移动或存在。

branches.en: THE IMMEDIACY: busy with something and about to do something are both close at hand.
branches.cn: 临近线：忙于某事与即将做某事，都表示贴近眼前。

intro.en: About is formed from two native English morphemes rather than from Latin parts.
intro.cn: about 由两个英语本族语素构成，而不是由拉丁构件拼成。

latinIntro.en: There is no direct Latin ancestor; the recorded Old English form is onbūtan.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有直接的拉丁语祖先；有文献记录的古英语形式是 onbūtan。

items.example: It appears in the Old English form onbūtan.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在古英语形式 onbūtan 中。

items.example: It is related to modern but.
items.exampleCN: 它与现代英语的 but 同源。

items.example: This form is the recorded ancestor.
items.exampleCN: 这个形式是有记录的前身。

items.example: It shows the ending that later disappeared.
items.exampleCN: 它显示了后来消失的词尾。

items.example: It survives unchanged in modern English.
items.exampleCN: 它在现代英语中原样保留下来。

items.example: The policy did an about-face.
items.exampleCN: 这项政策来了一次彻底转向。

items.example: They took a roundabout route.
items.exampleCN: 他们走了一条绕远的路线。

items.example: It cost ten pounds or thereabout.
items.exampleCN: 它花了十英镑左右。

环岛；迂回说法
大约；在那附近

definition_zh: 在……上方；高于；超过；上述的；上文；不屑于
definition_en: in or to a higher position than something, more than a number or standard, or earlier in a piece of writing
core_image: 一盏灯悬在桌面之上，光从高处落下来
scene: 厨房的灯吊在长桌上方，桌面上摊着面粉和擀面杖。The lamp hangs above the table, just out of reach.
sceneCN: 这里 above 指在……上方（第 1 个义项：位置高于某物）；句意为灯挂在桌子上方，刚好够不到。

derivatives.zh: 由 above 加 board 构成，义为「光明正大的；公开的」
由 above 加 mentioned 构成，义为「上述的」
由 above 加 ground 构成，义为「地面上的」

senses.title: Higher than something
senses.definition: in a position that is higher than a stated object or point
senses.definitionCN: 处于比某个指定物体或位置更高的地方
senses.example: The lamp hangs above the table, just out of reach.
senses.exampleCN: 灯挂在桌子上方，刚好够不到。
senses.why: Old English bufan meant over, and the word has always been a simple statement of height.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 bufan 意为「在上方」，这个词一直只是对高度的简单陈述。

senses.title: Higher in rank
senses.definition: of greater rank, authority or importance than another person
senses.definitionCN: 在等级、权力或重要性上高于另一人
senses.example: Only the officers above him could change the order.
senses.exampleCN: 只有他上级的军官才能更改这道命令。
senses.why: Height became a picture of rank: those higher up stand physically above in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 高度变成了等级的画面：位高之人在想象中也站得更高。

senses.title: More than a number
senses.definition: greater than a stated amount, price or temperature
senses.definitionCN: 大于某个指定数量、价格或温度
senses.example: The temperature stayed above thirty all week.
senses.exampleCN: 整整一周气温都在三十度以上。
senses.why: On a scale, anything higher is literally above the line, so quantity followed position.
senses.whyCN: 在刻度上，更高的东西字面上就在那条线之上，于是数量义跟随位置义而来。

senses.title: Better than a standard
senses.definition: of a quality or performance, better than what is normal or required
senses.definitionCN: 指品质或表现优于正常或要求的水平
senses.example: Her work is well above the standard for the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她的作业远高于班级的标准。
senses.why: A standard is a line, and excellence sits above it.
senses.whyCN: 标准是一条线，而优秀就坐在线的上方。

senses.title: Earlier in a text
senses.definition: used to refer to something written earlier on the same page or document
senses.definitionCN: 用来指同一页或同一文件中前面写到的东西
senses.example: The figures above show the change over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 上文的数字显示了十年间的变化。
senses.why: A page is read from top to bottom, so what is higher on the page was said earlier.
senses.whyCN: 书页从上往下读，因此页面上更靠上的内容就是更早说过的内容。

senses.title: Too good to do something
senses.definition: in above doing something, too honourable or proud to do it
senses.definitionCN: 在 above doing 结构中，指品格太高或太骄傲而不屑去做
senses.example: She is above taking credit for other people's work.
senses.exampleCN: 她不屑于把别人的成果算在自己头上。
senses.why: Moral height works like physical height: a person above a small act cannot stoop to it.
senses.whyCN: 道德高度与物理高度同理：高于某种小动作的人，不会俯身去做。

intro.en: Above is an old English compound of on and over. Its physical sense of height produced rank, quantity, text order and moral distance.
intro.cn: above 是古英语中「在」与「在上」的复合词。它的物理高度义衍生出等级、数量、文本顺序与道德距离。

items.en: Above all and above average are fixed phrases, and the above is a common way to refer back to earlier text.
items.cn: above all 与 above average 是固定短语，the above 是回指前文的常见说法。

items.en: The form settled as above, and it began to be used for rank and for earlier passages in a book.
items.cn: 词形固定为 above，并开始用于等级以及书中靠前的段落。

items.en: Abufan combined a- on with bufan above, and described position over a thing.
items.cn: abufan 由 a-「在」与 bufan「在上」组合而成，描述在某物之上的位置。

items.en: Bufan itself came from be- by and ufan above, a doubled picture of height.
items.cn: bufan 本身由 be-「靠」与 ufan「在上」构成，是「高度」的双重画面。

items.en: The root uf- meant up, and it survives in English up and in German auf.
items.cn: 词根 uf- 意为「向上」，保存在英语 up 与德语 auf 中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers short place words that are easily confused with above; the near-meaning group gathers words of higher position and greater amount.
note.cn: 形近组收容易与 above 混淆的短方位词；近义组收表示更高位置与更大数量的词。

entries.definition: Concerning, or roughly.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「关于；大约」，与 above 只差一个字母。

entries.definition: On or onto a ship or vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「在船上；上车」，拼写相近但指交通工具。

entries.definition: Open and honest.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「光明正大的」，由 above 加 board 构成。

entries.definition: At a higher level than something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……上方」，与 above 语义重叠最多。

entries.definition: Toward a higher place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「向上」，与 above 同出 uf- 词根。

entries.definition: Directly across or higher than.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在正上方；越过」，常可与 above 互换。

entries.definition: At a greater height or level.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词比较级，义为「更高的」。

entries.definition: Further than a point or limit.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「超出」，对应数量与限度义。

entries.definition: Greater than a stated amount.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「超过的」，书面色彩强。

entries.definition: Better or higher in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「更高的；更优的」，对应等级义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of a lamp hanging over a table.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「一盏灯吊在桌子上方」这一画面。

normal.en: Above contains over in its meaning: both look down from a higher place.
normal.cn: above 的含义里藏着 over：两者都从更高的位置往下看。

normal.en: A page is read downward, so what is above was said first.
normal.cn: 书页从上往下读，所以上面的内容是最先说的。

normal.en: Above average means your mark sits on the upper side of the line.
normal.cn: above average 意味着你的分数坐在那条线的上侧。

normal.en: Above all puts one thing at the very top of the list.
normal.cn: above all 把一件事放到清单的最顶端。

normal.en: Above taking credit means the person will not stoop that low.
normal.cn: above taking credit 意味着那个人不肯俯身到那么低。

abstract.en: Picture a light fixture fixed to the ceiling, shining down on everything below.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏固定在天花板上的灯，向下照着他下面的一切。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps height: in space, in rank, in number, in the page, in morals, in heaven.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留高度：空间中的、等级中的、数量上的、书页上的、道德上的、天上的。

abstract.en: The root uf- simply means up, and up is the whole story of the word.
abstract.cn: 词根 uf- 只表示「向上」，而「向上」就是这个词的全部故事。

examples.en: The lamp hangs above the table, just out of reach.
examples.cn: 灯挂在桌子上方，刚好够不到。

examples.en: Her work is well above the standard for the class.
examples.cn: 她的作业远高于班级的标准。

examples.en: The figures above show the change over ten years.
examples.cn: 上文的数字显示了十年间的变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄巴夫」——厄巴把灯举到头顶，光从高处洒下来

root: 古英语 ufan「在上」→ bufan「在上方」→ abufan「在……之上」→ 英语 above。核心是「高度」：空间在上、等级在上、数量在上、书页在上、道德在上、天堂在上。

sensesIntro.en: Six senses lift one position: over a place, over a rank, over a number, over a standard, earlier in a text, and beyond one's dignity.
sensesIntro.cn: 六个义项都在抬高位置：高于地点、高于等级、超过数目、超过标准、位于上文，以及不屑于去做。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lamp hanging above a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一盏灯悬在桌子之上。

branches.en: THE SPACE: higher than a point or surface.
branches.cn: 空间线：高于某个点或面。

branches.en: THE RANK: higher in status or authority.
branches.cn: 等级线：地位或权力更高。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: more than a stated amount.
branches.cn: 数量线：多于所说的数目。

branches.en: THE STANDARD: better than a required level.
branches.cn: 标准线：优于所要求的水准。

branches.en: THE PRIORITY: what is written earlier stands higher, and what is beneath one is refused.
branches.cn: 优先线：写在前面位置更高，而不屑去做的事被置于身下。

items.example: It combines with ufan to make bufan.

definition_zh: 并排；并肩；不落后；及时了解
definition_en: side by side, level with another, or keeping fully up to date
core_image: 几个人肩并肩排成一条横线，谁也没有超前，谁也没有掉队
scene: 海风很大，三艘小船保持着同一速度，船头排成一条横线。The two runners stayed abreast for the whole final lap.
sceneCN: 这里 abreast 指两人并排同速前进（第 1 个义项：并排成线）；句意为两名跑者整圈都保持并肩。

pos.zh: 并排地；并肩地；不落后地

derivatives.zh: 同根单纯词，义为「胸部；船的前部」
由 breast 与 bone 合成，义为「胸骨」
由 breast 与 stroke 合成，义为「蛙泳」

senses.title: Side by side in a line
senses.definition: placed side by side on the same line
senses.definitionCN: 并排放在同一条线上
senses.example: The guards stood abreast at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 卫兵并排站在大门旁。
senses.why: A breast is the front of the body, so abreast means front to front along one line.
senses.whyCN: breast 是身体的前部，因此 abreast 就是正面朝前排成一线。

senses.title: Level with a rival in a race
senses.definition: at the same distance in a race, with no one ahead
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中距离相同，没有人领先
senses.example: The two horses ran abreast down the straight.
senses.exampleCN: 两匹马在直道上并排奔驰。
senses.why: Competitors side by side are measured against the same line.
senses.whyCN: 并排的竞争者，是以同一条线为尺度。

senses.title: Keeping up with news
senses.definition: having the latest information about something
senses.definitionCN: 掌握某事的最新信息
senses.example: She reads two papers to keep abreast of the news.
senses.exampleCN: 她读两份报纸以紧跟新闻。
senses.why: To keep abreast is to stay level with events that keep moving forward.
senses.whyCN: keep abreast 就是与不断向前的事件保持齐平。

intro.en: Abreast is a nautical word made from a preposition and a body part, and it has travelled from ships to news.
intro.cn: abreast 是个航海词，由一个介词和一个身体部位词构成，后来从船只走到了新闻。

items.en: In modern usage the phrase keep abreast of dominates, and the physical sense survives mainly at sea.
items.cn: 在现代用法中，keep abreast of 占主导，具体的并排义主要留在海上。

items.en: Newspapers made keeping abreast a matter of reading, not of rowing, and the word entered ordinary prose.
items.cn: 报纸让 keeping abreast 变成阅读的事，而不是划船的事，这个词由此进入日常文章。

items.en: Sixteenth-century sailing accounts use abreast for ships lying side by side on the same line.
items.cn: 十六世纪的航海记述用 abreast 指船只并排处于同一条线上。

items.en: The noun breast meant the front of the body or the front of a ship, the surface that faces forward.
items.cn: 名词 breast 指身体的前部，也指船的前部，即朝前的那一面。

items.en: Old English brēost supplied the body-part noun; the prefix a- comes from on, meaning on or at.
items.cn: 古英语 brēost 提供了这个身体部位名词；前缀 a- 来自 on，意为「在……上」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the body-part noun and its compounds; the near-meaning group collects words for being level or informed.
note.cn: 形近组收身体部位名词及其复合词；近义组收表示「齐平」或「知情」的词。

entries.definition: The front of the body or of a ship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胸部；船的前部」。

entries.definition: The flat bone in the middle of the chest.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「胸骨」。

entries.definition: A swimming style with both arms moving together.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蛙泳」。

entries.definition: To feed a baby with milk from the breast.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「以母乳喂养」。

entries.definition: Next to and along the side of something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……旁边；与……并排」。

entries.definition: At the same height or standard.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「齐平的；同水平的」。

entries.definition: Knowing the latest facts about something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「了解情况的」。

entries.definition: Belonging to the present time.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「当前的」。

entries.definition: Running side by side at a fixed distance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「平行的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the nautical picture and the reading phrase that keeps the word alive.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子用航海的画面，以及让这个词活下来的阅读搭配。

normal.en: A plus breast: two people put their fronts on the same line.
normal.cn: a 加 breast：两个人把胸前的一面朝向同一条线。

normal.en: Ships lying abreast are level, and the phrase keep abreast of news borrows that level line.
normal.cn: 船并排就是齐平，keep abreast of 的消息义借用了这条齐平的线。

normal.en: The opposite of abreast is astern, behind the stern of another ship.
normal.cn: abreast 的反面是 astern，即落在另一艘船的船尾之后。

normal.en: Line abreast is a formation word: the whole row moves as one wall.
normal.cn: line abreast 是队形用语：整排像一堵墙一样移动。

normal.en: When you keep abreast of a field, you walk level with its fastest writers.
normal.cn: 当你 keep abreast of 某个领域，你就与该领域最快的写作者并肩而行。

abstract.en: Picture a row of walkers roped together: the rope is the line, and abreast means no one has slack.
abstract.cn: 想象一排用绳子连着的行走者：绳子就是那条线，abreast 意味着谁都没有松绳。

abstract.en: Cut the rope and the same picture explains news: a fast-moving line of events, and you must stay level with it.
abstract.cn: 把绳子剪断，同一画面也能解释新闻：事件是一条快速移动的线，你必须与它齐平。

abstract.en: Every sense asks one question: are you on the same line, or are you behind?
abstract.cn: 所有义项都在问同一个问题：你是在同一条线上，还是落在了后面？

examples.en: The two boats moved abreast into the harbour.
examples.cn: 两条船并排驶入港口。

examples.en: Readers should keep abreast of new findings.
examples.cn: 读者应当及时了解新的发现。

examples.en: The runners were abreast at the halfway mark.
examples.cn: 跑者们在半程处并排。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布瑞斯特」——阿布和瑞斯特并肩走，谁也不肯落后半步

root: 由 a-（on「在……上」）+ breast（古英语 brēost「胸部；船的前部」）构成，字面义为「以胸前一线并排」。十六世纪航海文献用它描写两船同线并行；十九世纪报刊把 keep abreast of 转用于「跟上消息」，遂有「不落后、及时了解」的抽象义。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses place things or people side by side, level in a race, and level with the latest news.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项把人和物并排放着：并排、比赛中齐平，以及与最新消息齐平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two bodies placed front to front on one horizontal line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个身体正面朝前，落在同一条水平线上。

branches.en: THE LINE: two bodies moving side by side.
branches.cn: 并排线：两个身体并着移动。

branches.en: THE RACE: level with a rival.
branches.cn: 竞赛线：与对手齐平。

branches.en: THE NEWS: level with what is happening now.
branches.cn: 消息线：与当下发生的事齐平。

branches.en: THE SIDE BY SIDE: physical alignment is the base of the racing sense.
branches.cn: 并肩线：身体对齐是竞赛义的底子。

branches.en: THE SYNC: keeping up with a neighbour and keeping up with events share one picture.
branches.cn: 同步线：跟上旁边的人与跟上时事，共用一幅画面。

intro.en: Abreast is built from an English prefix and an English noun, so its parts are native rather than borrowed.
intro.cn: abreast 由英语前缀与英语名词构成，构件属本族语而非借词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin ancestor is recorded for this nautical formation; the parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个航海构词没有拉丁语祖先的记录，其构件来自古英语。

items.exampleCN: 它出现在 aboard 和 abreast 中。

items.example: It also means the front of a ship.
items.exampleCN: 它也可指船的前部。

items.example: The recorded form supplies the modern noun.
items.exampleCN: 有记录的形式提供了现代名词。

items.example: It began as a sailing term.
items.exampleCN: 它起初是航海术语。

items.example: The breastbone protects the heart.
items.exampleCN: 胸骨保护心脏。

items.example: She swims breaststroke every morning.
items.exampleCN: 她每天早上游蛙泳。

items.example: Mothers may breastfeed in this room.
items.exampleCN: 母亲们可以在这个房间哺乳。

items.example: The soldier wore a breastplate.
items.exampleCN: 士兵穿着护胸甲。

definition_zh: 在国外；到国外；广泛流传；在户外（古义）；遍布
definition_en: in or to a foreign country, or spread widely among many people
core_image: 一个人提着行李走出国境线，身后的路一下子变宽
scene: 机场的到达口，行李箱排成一列，接机牌上写着陌生的城市名。She went abroad to study medicine and stayed for six years.
sceneCN: 这里 abroad 指到国外（第 1 个义项：离开本国去外国）；句意为她出国学医，一待就是六年。

pos.zh: 副词：在国外；到国外；广泛流传

derivatives.zh: 与本词同源的形容词，义为「宽的；广阔的」
由 broad 加 -th 构成，义为「宽度；广度」
由 broad 加 -en 构成，义为「拓宽；扩大」

senses.title: In a foreign country
senses.definition: living or staying in a country that is not your own
senses.definitionCN: 在并非自己国家的土地上生活或停留
senses.example: She went abroad to study medicine and stayed for six years.
senses.exampleCN: 她出国学医，一待就是六年。
senses.why: Old English on brade meant in the broad, and being out in the wide world came to mean being outside your own country.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 on brade 意为「在广阔之处」，置身于广阔世界后来就指身处本国之外。

senses.title: To a foreign country
senses.definition: moving or travelling out of your own country
senses.definitionCN: 离开本国到外国去
senses.example: The firm sends young engineers abroad for training.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把年轻工程师派往国外培训。
senses.why: The same adverb covers position and movement, because English often does not mark the difference.
senses.whyCN: 同一个副词兼具位置与移动，因为英语常常不标记二者的差别。

senses.title: Widely spread among people
senses.definition: of news, rumours or ideas, circulating among many people
senses.definitionCN: 指消息、传言或观念在很多人中间流传
senses.example: Rumours of the merger were already abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 合并的传言早已四处流传。
senses.why: To be abroad is to be out in the open and everywhere, so a story abroad has escaped its source.
senses.whyCN: abroad 就是「在外面、到处」，因此一则 abroad 的消息已经离开了它的源头。

intro.en: Abroad first meant simply out in the broad open. From outdoors it moved to foreign countries and to ideas spreading widely.
intro.cn: abroad 最初只表示「在开阔的户外」。它从户外走向外国，也走向广泛传播的观念。

items.en: Abroad is now mainly a word for foreign travel, and study abroad is a standard phrase in education.
items.cn: abroad 如今主要指国外旅行，study abroad 已成为教育领域的标准说法。

items.en: The sense of being outside one's country became dominant, while the outdoor sense faded into older prose.
items.cn: 「身处本国之外」的含义成为主导，而户外的含义退入较早的散文。

items.en: The form abrode appeared, still meaning out in the open or at a distance.
items.cn: 中古英语出现 abrode 这一形式，仍表示「在开阔处」或「在远处」。

items.en: The phrase on bræde meant in the broad, built from on and brad broad.
items.cn: 短语 on bræde 意为「在广阔之处」，由 on「在」与 brad「宽的」构成。

items.en: Brad meant broad, and it also gives English broad and breadth, so the root picture is open width.
items.cn: brad 意为「宽的」，还产生英语的 broad 与 breadth，词根画面就是开阔的宽度。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers broad-root words and a misleading near spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words for foreign places and wide spread.
note.cn: 形近组收 broad 词根与一个易混近形词；近义组收表示异国与广泛传播的词。

entries.definition: Wide from side to side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽的」，abroad 的词根来源。

entries.definition: The distance from one side to the other.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「宽度；广度」。

entries.definition: To make or become wider.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「拓宽；扩大」。

entries.definition: On a ship, train or aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「在交通工具上」，与 abroad 只差一个字母。

entries.definition: A home or a place of residence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「住所」，拼写近似但含义无关。

entries.definition: In or to a country across the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 副词与形容词，义为「在海外；海外的」，与 abroad 最接近。

entries.definition: Belonging to another country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「外国的」，修饰名词时对应 abroad 的位置义。

entries.definition: At a distance from a place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「离开；在远处」，对应「离家在外」义。

entries.definition: Over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「广泛地」，对应「流传」义。

entries.definition: Not inside a building.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「在户外」，对应古义。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of stepping out through a gate into a wide space.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「走出大门、来到开阔之地」这一画面。

normal.en: Abroad contains broad: the world outside is wide.
normal.cn: abroad 里藏着 broad：外面的世界是宽的。

normal.en: A broad road leads out of the country.
normal.cn: 一条宽阔的路通向国门之外。

normal.en: Rumours abroad have escaped the room where they started.
normal.cn: 流传在外的传言，已经逃出了它最初的那间屋子。

normal.en: Aboard is on the ship, abroad is beyond the shore: one letter, two worlds.
normal.cn: aboard 在船上，abroad 在岸外：一个字母，两个世界。

normal.en: Study abroad means the classroom moved to another country.
normal.cn: study abroad 意味着教室搬到了另一个国家。

abstract.en: Picture a door opening onto a plain with no fences in sight.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门打开，外面是一片看不到篱笆的旷野。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps breadth: wide land, wide travel, wide spread, wide imagination.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留「宽广」：宽广的土地、宽广的旅行、宽广的传播、宽广的想象。

abstract.en: The oldest sense is the open air, and the modern sense is simply that openness at national scale.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义是露天的开阔，现代含义只是把这份开阔放大到国家尺度。

examples.en: She went abroad to study medicine and stayed for six years.

examples.en: Rumours of the merger were already abroad.
examples.cn: 合并的传言早已四处流传。

examples.en: The firm sends young engineers abroad for training.
examples.cn: 公司把年轻工程师派往国外培训。

root: 古英语 brad「宽的」→ on bræde「在广阔处」→ abrode → 英语 abroad。核心是「开阔」：户外的开阔、异国的开阔、消息传开的开阔、想象越界的开阔。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses cover being in another country, going to another country, and spreading widely.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项覆盖身在国外、前往国外，以及广泛传开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person steps through a gate into wide open space.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人走出大门，来到开阔的空间。

branches.en: THE PLACE: one is outside one's own country.
branches.cn: 地点线：人在本国之外。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION: one goes out of the country.
branches.cn: 方向线：人往国外去。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: news or a custom travels far.
branches.cn: 传播线：消息或风俗传得很远。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE: place and direction share one boundary crossed.
branches.cn: 在外线：地点与方向共用同一条被跨过的边界。

branches.en: THE WIDE WORLD: abroad can mean anywhere far from home.
branches.cn: 广远线：abroad 也可以指离家很远的地方。

intro.en: Abroad is an Old English prepositional phrase frozen into an adverb, built on the root for broad.
intro.cn: abroad 是一个凝固成副词的古英语介词短语，建立在表示「宽」的词根上。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is brad, on bræde and abroad.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 brad、on bræde 与 abroad。

items.exampleCN: 它还产生 broad 与 breadth。

items.example: It opens the phrase on bræde.

items.example: It supplies the wide image.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「开阔」这一意象。

items.example: It is the earlier form of abroad.

items.example: It is the modern form.

items.example: It remains at the front of abroad.
items.exampleCN: 它留在 abroad 的开头。

items.example: It is the living relative of brad.
items.exampleCN: 它是 brad 的现代亲缘词。

items.example: It comes from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 它同出这一词根。

definition_zh: 突然的；意外的；陡峭的；唐突的；不连贯的
definition_en: happening suddenly, rising almost vertically, or short and rude in manner
core_image: 一堵石壁从平地上骤然立起，没有过渡的缓坡
scene: 山路走到一半，前面的石壁忽然直上直下，连个缓坡都没有。The path came to an abrupt end at the edge of the cliff.
sceneCN: 这里 abrupt 指道路陡然到头（第 5 个义项：戛然而止）；句意为小路在崖边突然中断。

pos.zh: 突然的；陡峭的；唐突的；不连贯的

senses.title: Sudden and unexpected
senses.definition: happening without any warning, so that it surprises people
senses.definitionCN: 毫无预警地发生，令人措手不及
senses.example: The war ended in an abrupt ceasefire.
senses.exampleCN: 战争在一场突然的停火中结束。
senses.why: Latin abruptus meant broken off, and a thing broken off stops without a slope or a warning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abruptus 意为「折断的」，被折断的东西停下时既没有斜坡也没有预告。

senses.title: Steep, almost vertical
senses.definition: rising or falling at a very sharp angle, with little slope
senses.definitionCN: 以很陡的角度上升或下降，几乎没有斜坡
senses.example: The trail climbed an abrupt wall of rock.
senses.exampleCN: 小路攀上一道陡直的石壁。
senses.why: A cliff is earth broken off, and the break leaves a face that is nearly upright.
senses.whyCN: 悬崖就是被折断的土地，断口留下一面近乎直立的壁。

senses.title: Curt and unfriendly in manner
senses.definition: speaking in a way that is short and seems rude
senses.definitionCN: 说话简短，显得没有礼貌
senses.example: His abrupt tone made the room go quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 他唐突的语气让整个房间安静下来。
senses.why: Speech cut off short feels like a conversation broken in the middle, which is why the word carries offence.
senses.whyCN: 把话截短，就像对话被人从中间折断，因此这个词带着冒犯感。

senses.title: Lacking smooth connections
senses.definition: moving from one point to another without smooth links, as in writing or music
senses.definitionCN: 在文章或音乐中从一个点跳到另一点，缺少平滑的衔接
senses.example: The essay has an abrupt shift in the third paragraph.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章在第三段有一处突兀的转折。
senses.why: Style that breaks off leaves a seam the reader can feel, the same seam as a broken stick.
senses.whyCN: 断裂的文气留下读者能感觉到的接缝，就像折断的树枝留下的断口。

senses.title: Coming to a sudden stop
senses.definition: ending or halting immediately, with no slowing down first
senses.definitionCN: 立刻结束或停住，事先没有任何减速
senses.example: The music stopped with an abrupt final chord.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐以一个突兀的终止和弦停下。
senses.why: The image is a moving thing that meets a wall rather than a slope.
senses.whyCN: 画面是一个移动的东西撞上了墙，而不是遇上斜坡。

intro.en: Abrupt is a Latin word for something broken off, brought to English through French, and every sense keeps that image of a clean break.
intro.cn: abrupt 是拉丁语中表示「被折断」的词，经法语进入英语，每个义项都保留着干净断口的意象。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word from slopes and stops to manners and style, always with the same lack of transition.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词从坡面与停顿扩展到态度与文风，但始终是同样的「没有过渡」。

items.en: Writers on landscape applied abrupt to cliffs and rock faces that rise without a gradual slope.
items.cn: 写地貌的作者把 abrupt 用于没有缓坡、陡然升起的崖壁与岩面。

items.en: English took the word from French abrupt in the sixteenth century, first describing steep ground and cut-off speech.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从法语 abrupt 借入这个词，最初描写陡峭的地面与被截断的话语。

items.en: Latin abruptus was the past participle of abrumpere, meaning broken off or torn away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abruptus 是 abrumpere 的过去分词，意为「被折断、被撕离」。

items.en: The verb rumpere meant to break and also produced rupture, erupt, and interrupt.
items.cn: 动词 rumpere 意为「折断」，还产生了 rupture、erupt、interrupt 等词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and words from the same breaking root; the near-meaning group collects words for suddenness, steepness, and curtness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「折断」词根的形式与同族词；近义组收表示突然、陡峭与简短无礼的词。

entries.definition: In a sudden or curt way.

entries.definition: The quality of being sudden, steep, or curt.

entries.definition: A break or burst, especially in a pipe or a relationship.
