entries.definition: To burst out, as a volcano does.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「喷发；爆发」，同出 rumpere 一词根。

entries.definition: Happening quickly and without warning.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「突然的」，强调发生得快。

entries.definition: Rising or falling at a sharp angle.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「陡的」，强调坡度大。

entries.definition: Short in a way that seems rude.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简短失礼的」。

entries.definition: Direct to the point of rudeness.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「直率到近乎粗鲁的」。

entries.definition: Done too quickly, without enough thought.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「仓促的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin picture of a stick snapped in two and the situations where the word appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「树枝被折成两段」的拉丁画面，以及这个词常出现的情境。

normal.en: Ab plus rupt: rupt means break, so abrupt is something broken off cleanly.
normal.cn: ab 加 rupt：rupt 意为折断，所以 abrupt 就是干脆被折断的东西。

normal.en: Think of a branch snapped over a knee: no slope, no warning, just a break.
normal.cn: 想象一根树枝在膝盖上被折断：没有斜坡，没有预告，只有断口。

normal.en: An abrupt reply is a sentence with its tail cut off.
normal.cn: abrupt 的回答，就是被切掉尾巴的句子。

normal.en: An abrupt cliff is the same break seen from the side, standing upright.
normal.cn: 陡崖就是同一个断口从侧面看，直立着。

normal.en: The family of words proves the root: rupture, erupt, interrupt all contain rupt.
normal.cn: 同族词可以证明这个词根：rupture、erupt、interrupt 都含 rupt。

abstract.en: Picture a line that ends not in a curve but in a cut: every sense of abrupt is that cut.
abstract.cn: 想象一条线不是以弧线收尾，而是被切断：abrupt 的每个义项都是那道切口。

abstract.en: Slope, speech, music, weather: in each, the missing transition is the thing you notice.
abstract.cn: 坡度、言语、音乐、天气：在每一处，你注意到的都是缺失的那段过渡。

abstract.en: The word is about absence of middle ground, not about speed.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的是中间地带的缺席，而不是速度。

examples.en: The meeting came to an abrupt end.
examples.cn: 会议突然结束了。

examples.en: There was an abrupt change in the weather.
examples.cn: 天气发生了突变。

examples.en: His abrupt reply surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 他生硬的回答让大家都吃了一惊。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ rumpere（折断）→ abruptus「被折断的、陡然的」；经法语 abrupt 进入英语。断口没有过渡，故有「突然、陡峭」义；话语像被切断，故有「唐突、简短生硬」义。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses share a break with no transition: in time, in a slope, in manner, in writing, and at an ending.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项共享「没有过渡的断裂」：时间上、坡度上、举止上、文气上，以及结尾处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stick snapped in two, leaving a hard edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被折成两段的树枝，留下生硬的断口。

branches.en: THE TIME: something happens with no warning.
branches.cn: 时间线：事情毫无预兆地发生。

branches.en: THE SLOPE: the ground falls away without a curve.
branches.cn: 地形线：地面没有弧度地陡然落下。

branches.en: THE MANNER: speech cuts off politeness.
branches.cn: 举止线：说话把礼貌截断了。

branches.en: THE WRITING: a style jumps where it should glide.
branches.cn: 文气线：该平滑过渡处却跳了一下。

branches.en: THE ENDING: a thing stops without being finished.
branches.cn: 终止线：事情没说完就停住。

intro.cn: abrupt 由一个拉丁前缀和一个拉丁动词构成，构件在同族英语词中仍然看得见。

latinIntro.en: The recorded Latin forms are abruptus, abrumpere, and rumpere; the prefix ab- means away.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的拉丁形式是 abruptus、abrumpere 与 rumpere；前缀 ab- 意为「离开」。

items.exampleCN: 它的分词形式变成了 abruptus。

items.example: His abruptness offended the guests.
items.exampleCN: 他的唐突冒犯了客人。

items.example: The pipe suffered a rupture.
items.exampleCN: 管道发生了破裂。

latinEntries.example: It is the direct source of French abrupt.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是法语 abrupt 的直接来源。

definition_en: the state of being away, or the lack of something that might be expected
core_image: 一把椅子空着，本该坐在上面的人不在
scene: 教室里那把椅子一直空着，点名时没有人应答。Her absence from the meeting was noticed by everyone.
sceneCN: 这里 absence 指人不在场（第 1 个义项：不在场）；句意为所有人都注意到她没有到会。

senses.title: The state of being away
senses.definition: the condition of not being in the place where one is usually expected
senses.definitionCN: 不在通常应该出现的那个地方
senses.example: His absence from the office lasted three days.
senses.exampleCN: 他有三天没到办公室。
senses.why: Latin absentia is built from abesse, to be away, and the noun simply names that state.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absentia 由 abesse「不在」构成，这个名词只是给那种状态命名。

senses.title: Failure to attend
senses.definition: not attending a class, meeting, or duty that one was expected to attend
senses.definitionCN: 没有参加本应参加的课、会议或职责
senses.example: Three absences will fail the course.
senses.exampleCN: 缺课三次就会不及格。
senses.why: Attendance is a row of seats, and an absence is a seat that stays empty.
senses.whyCN: 出勤是一排座位，缺席就是一直空着的那一个。

senses.title: Lack of something
senses.definition: the state of not having something that would normally be present
senses.definitionCN: 缺少本应存在的东西
senses.example: The absence of rain has hurt the crops.
senses.exampleCN: 缺少雨水已经损害了庄稼。
senses.why: The same noun covers people and things: whatever should be in a place and is not is absent.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既管人也管物：本该在某处却不在的，就是缺席。

senses.title: The state of not existing
senses.definition: the fact that something does not exist at all in a given situation
senses.definitionCN: 某事物在特定情形下根本不存在
senses.example: There is an absence of any written record.
senses.exampleCN: 完全没有任何书面记录存在。
senses.why: When the missing thing never existed, the empty chair is not a gap but a silence.
senses.whyCN: 当缺少的东西从未存在，空椅子就不是一个缺口，而是一片沉默。

intro.en: Absence comes from the Latin verb to be away, and it names a place or a moment where something should have been.
intro.cn: absence 出自拉丁语中表示「不在」的动词，它命名的是一处或一段时间里本该有某物的地方。

items.en: Modern English uses the noun for people, things, and evidence, so that an absence can be an argument in itself.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个名词用于人、物与证据，于是「缺席」本身也能成为论据。

items.en: Middle English borrowed absence through French and used it for both the state of being away and the lack of a quality.
items.cn: 中古英语经法语借入 absence，既指人不在，也指某种品质的缺乏。

items.en: Old French absence carried the Latin noun into everyday use for courtly and legal contexts.
items.cn: 古法语 absence 把这个拉丁名词带入宫廷与法律场合的日常使用。

items.en: Latin absentia was a noun of state formed from the present participle of abesse.
items.cn: 拉丁语 absentia 是由 abesse 的现在分词构成的状态名词。

items.en: Abesse combined ab, away, with esse, to be: literally to be away from a place.
items.cn: abesse 把表示离开的 ab 与表示存在的 esse 组合起来，字面就是「从某处不在」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on the same absent root; the near-meaning group collects nouns for lack and for not attending.
note.cn: 形近组收由同一 absent 词根构成的词；近义组收表示缺乏与未出席的名词。

entries.definition: Not present in a place.

entries.definition: In a distracted, inattentive way.

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「空缺；空房」。

entries.definition: An empty space between two things or a missing part.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺口；间隔」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin parts of the word and the empty-seat picture that every sense shares.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用这个词真实的拉丁构件，以及所有义项共有的「空椅子」画面。

normal.en: Ab plus esse: esse means to be, and ab means away, so absence is to be away.
normal.cn: ab 加 esse：esse 意为存在，ab 意为离开，所以 absence 就是「不在那里」。

normal.en: The adverb absently shows the inner version: the body sits in the chair, the mind does not.
normal.cn: 副词 absently 显示内在版本：身体坐在椅子上，心思却没在。

normal.en: Keep the pair in order: absent is the adjective, absence is the noun, absentee is the person.
normal.cn: 把这一组按顺序记：absent 是形容词，absence 是名词，absentee 是人。

normal.en: Leave of absence is a legal phrase, so the word appears on forms as well as in sad sentences.
normal.cn: leave of absence 是法律短语，所以这个词既出现在表格上，也出现在悲伤的句子里。

normal.en: In the absence of evidence is a common phrase: the missing thing itself becomes the argument.
normal.cn: in the absence of evidence 很常见：缺失的东西本身成了论据。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled out from a table: the table keeps the shape of the missing chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子从桌边被抽走：桌子仍保留着那把椅子留下的形状。

abstract.en: Every sense reads that shape: a person, a thing, a quality, or a record that should fill it and does not.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在读这个形状：本该填满它的人、物、品质或记录，却没有出现。

abstract.en: The word is powerful because a hole can be as visible as a stone.
abstract.cn: 这个词有力量，是因为一个洞也可以像石头一样可见。

examples.cn: 所有人都注意到她没有到会。

examples.en: The absence of clean water is the village's main problem.
examples.cn: 缺少干净的水是这个村子最主要的问题。

examples.en: He took a leave of absence to care for his father.
examples.cn: 他请假去照顾父亲。

senses.title: Not at school or work

intro.en: Absent comes from a Latin verb meaning to be away. It began as plain not-being-there and grew senses of lack and distraction.
intro.cn: absent 来自一个意为「不在」的拉丁动词。它从朴素的「不在那里」生长出「缺乏」与「走神」的含义。

items.en: Absent is used for school, work and court, and absent-minded became a common word for a distracted person.
items.cn: absent 用于学校、工作与法庭，absent-minded 成为形容走神者的常用词。

items.en: Compulsory schooling made absent a daily word, and registers recorded who was away.
items.cn: 义务教育使 absent 成为日常词，点名册记录着谁没来。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective from French and Latin, using it for people and later for qualities.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语从法语与拉丁语借入这个形容词，先用于人，后用于品质。

items.en: Absens was the present participle of abesse, to be away, and it named anyone not in a place.
items.cn: absens 是 abesse「不在」的现在分词，指任何不在某处的人。

items.en: Esse, to be, supplies the verb at the heart of the word, so absence is a way of being rather than a thing.
items.cn: esse「存在」提供这个词核心的动词，因此缺席是一种存在方式，而不是一件东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the absence family and its opposite; the near-meaning group gathers words for missing, lacking and distracted.
note.cn: 形近组收 absence 词族及反义词；近义组收表示缺失、缺乏与走神的词。

entries.definition: The state of being away.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席；缺乏」。

entries.definition: A person who is not present.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺席者」。

entries.definition: In a distracted way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「心不在焉地」。

entries.definition: Often forgetting things because the mind is elsewhere.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「心不在焉的」。

entries.definition: In the place being talked about.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「在场的」，是本词的反义。

entries.definition: Not found in the expected place.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「失踪的；缺失的」，最接近。

entries.definition: Not in the usual place.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「不在；在外」，对应不在场义。

entries.definition: Not present in the necessary amount.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「缺乏的」，对应品质缺失义。

entries.definition: Unable to keep attention on one thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「分心的」，对应走神义。

entries.definition: Empty and unused.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「空的；无人占用的」，常指座位或职位。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of a roll call with an empty seat.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些联想用「点名时出现空座位」这一画面。

normal.en: Absent is ab- plus sent: the person was sent away from the room.
normal.cn: absent 可看作 ab- 加 sent：人被打发离开房间。

normal.en: Absence is the noun, absentee is the person, absently is the manner.
normal.cn: absence 是状态，absentee 是人，absently 是方式。

normal.en: An absent look is a face whose owner has gone elsewhere.
normal.cn: absent look 是一张主人的神已经去了别处的脸。

normal.en: Absent from school is a roll-call word; absent father is an emotional one.
normal.cn: absent from school 是点名册上的词，absent father 是情感层面的词。

normal.en: To absent oneself is to choose the empty seat.
normal.cn: absent oneself 就是主动选择那个空座位。

abstract.en: Picture a name called out in a room where nobody answers.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋里有人喊出一个名字，却没有人应。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps an empty place: a desk, a room, a quality, a mind, a court, a record.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留一个空位：课桌、房间、品质、头脑、法庭、记录。

abstract.en: The root meaning is simply to be away, and every later sense is that awayness applied to something new.
abstract.cn: 词根含义只是「不在」，后来每个义项都是把这份「不在」用到新的对象上。

examples.en: Two pupils were absent from class today.
examples.cn: 今天有两名学生缺课。

examples.en: An absent look came over his face when she mentioned the name.
examples.cn: 她提到那个名字时，他脸上露出心不在焉的神情。

examples.en: He absented himself from the meeting without a word.
examples.cn: 他一句话没说就缺席了会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「厄布森特」——厄布被派到别处，座位上只剩一件外套

root: 拉丁语 abesse「不在」← ab-「离开」+ esse「存在」→ absens → 英语 absent。核心是「存在在别处」：缺课、不在场、缺乏、走神、主动避开、法庭缺席、情感缺席、记录中不存在。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses mark a person away from a place, a person away when expected, and a quality that is missing.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项分别标记人不在某处、该出现时不在，以及某种特质缺失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a roll call with an empty seat.
core.cn: 核心意象：点名时出现一个空座位。

branches.en: THE PERSON: someone is not at school or at work.
branches.cn: 人员线：某人不在学校或岗位。

branches.en: THE PLACE: someone is not where the others are.
branches.cn: 地点线：某人不在众人所在之处。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: a thing lacks a usual element.
branches.cn: 特质线：某物缺少惯有的成分。

branches.en: THE AWAY: both senses describe a body missing from a spot.
branches.cn: 不在线：两个义项都描述身体不在某个位置。

branches.en: THE MISSING PIECE: a missing person and a missing quality leave the same gap.
branches.cn: 缺位线：缺人与缺特质，留下的是同一种空。

intro.cn: absent 是拉丁语「不在」的现在分词，其词族涵盖名词、副词与注意力相关的复合词。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is esse, abesse and absens.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 esse、abesse 与 absens。

definition_zh: 绝对的；完全的；不受限制的；确实的
definition_en: complete and total, free from any limit or condition, or fixed in itself rather than relative
core_image: 一个已经松开所有绳索的东西，不再被任何条件牵住
scene: 实验室的温度计停在最底端，刻度之外再没有更低的数。At absolute zero, all molecular motion stops.
sceneCN: 这里 absolute 指理论上的最低温度极限（第 5 个义项：科学上的极限值）；句意为在绝对零度，一切分子运动都停止。

pos.zh: 绝对的；完全的；不受限制的；确实的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「绝对地；完全地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「绝对性；无条件性」
由形容词加 -ism 构成，义为「专制主义；绝对主义」
由 absolutism 派生，义为「专制主义者」
同出拉丁 absolvere，义为「赦免；免除责任」

senses.title: Complete and total
senses.definition: used to stress that a quality or state is complete, with nothing missing
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某种性质或状态完整无缺，一点不剩
senses.example: The room was in absolute darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里一片漆黑。
senses.why: Latin absolutus meant freed from every condition, so nothing outside it can limit how total it is.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absolutus 意为「从一切条件中解脱」，因此没有任何外部因素能限制它的彻底程度。

senses.title: Free from limits on power
senses.definition: holding power that no law, parliament, or rival can check
senses.definitionCN: 掌握着法律、议会或对手都无法制约的权力
senses.example: The king claimed absolute power over the courts.
senses.exampleCN: 国王宣称对法院拥有绝对权力。
senses.why: A ruler who is absolved from obligations stands outside the network of checks that binds others.
senses.whyCN: 被免除义务的统治者，站在约束他人的那张制衡之网之外。

senses.title: Not relative to anything
senses.definition: true or existing in itself, not measured against something else
senses.definitionCN: 自身成立或存在，不以他物为参照
senses.example: Philosophers argued about an absolute good.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家们争论是否存在绝对的善。
senses.why: The word's legal root is release from bonds, and a thing released from comparison stands alone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的法律词根是「从束缚中释放」，脱离比较的事物便独自立着。

senses.title: Definite and certain
senses.definition: so certain that no doubt or exception is possible
senses.definitionCN: 确定到不可能有疑问或例外
senses.example: She has absolute confidence in the result.
senses.exampleCN: 她对结果有绝对的信心。
senses.why: Certainty here is not high probability but the absence of any condition that could alter the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里的确定不是高概率，而是不存在任何能改变结果的条件。

senses.title: A scientific lower limit
senses.definition: the lowest temperature possible, at which particle motion is minimal
senses.definitionCN: 可能达到的最低温度，此时粒子运动降到最低
senses.example: The experiment was cooled to near absolute zero.
senses.exampleCN: 实验被冷却到接近绝对零度。
senses.why: Science borrowed the word for a limit that no condition can push past, the clearest modern use of the root idea.
senses.whyCN: 科学借这个词表示任何条件都推不过去的界限，这是词根观念最清楚的现代用法。

intro.en: Absolute comes from a Latin verb meaning to loosen or release, and its history moves from legal freedom to total power and to the ultimate.
intro.cn: absolute 出自拉丁语中表示「松开、释放」的动词，它的历史从法律上的免除走到完全的权力，再到终极实在。

items.en: Modern English uses absolute for total qualities, unchecked power, fixed values, and philosophical reality, all built on freedom from conditions.
items.cn: 现代英语用 absolute 表示完全的性质、不受制约的权力、固定的数值与哲学的实在，全都建立在「摆脱条件」之上。

items.en: Physicists gave the word a precise scale when they fixed absolute zero as the lowest possible temperature.
items.cn: 物理学家把绝对零度定为可能的最低温度，从此给了这个词一个精确的标尺。

items.en: Sixteenth-century political writing used absolute for a ruler released from the checks that bound other men.
items.cn: 十六世纪的政治写作把 absolute 用于不受约束他人之制衡的统治者。

items.en: Latin absolutus, the participle of absolvere, meant completed, freed, or released from an obligation.
items.cn: 拉丁语 absolutus 是 absolvere 的分词，意为「完成的、被释放的、免除义务的」。

items.en: Absolvere joined ab, away, with solvere, to loosen, giving the picture of ropes being untied.
items.cn: absolvere 把表示离开的 ab 与表示松开的 solvere 组合起来，画面就是绳索被解下。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same release root; the near-meaning group collects words for totality, certainty, and supreme power.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「释放」词根的词；近义组收表示完全、确定与最高权力的词。

entries.definition: Completely, or used as a strong yes or no.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「绝对地；完全地」，也可表示强烈的肯定或否定。

entries.definition: The quality of being complete or unconditional.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「绝对性；无条件性」。

entries.definition: A system in which one ruler holds unchecked power.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「专制主义；绝对主义」。

entries.definition: To declare someone free from blame or duty.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赦免；免除责任」，与 absolute 同出 absolvere。

entries.definition: Whole, with nothing missing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「完整的；完全的」。

entries.definition: Including everything, with no part left out.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「全部的；彻底的」。

entries.definition: Given or true without any conditions attached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无条件的」。

entries.definition: Clearly stated and not open to doubt.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「明确的；确定的」。

entries.definition: Holding the highest rank or power.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「最高的；至上的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin picture of untied ropes and the fixed phrases the word actually forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「绳索被解开」的拉丁画面，以及这个词实际构成的固定搭配。

normal.en: Ab plus solute: solute means loosened, so absolute is fully loosened, tied by nothing.
normal.cn: ab 加 solute：solute 意为松开的，所以 absolute 就是彻底松开、不被任何东西绑住。

normal.en: Absolute zero is the floor of the universe: nothing can go lower, so no condition can pull it further.
normal.cn: 绝对零度是宇宙的地板：没有东西能更低，也就没有条件能再把它往下拉。

normal.en: An absolute monarch is a king with the ropes cut, standing outside the web of checks.
normal.cn: absolute monarch 就是绳索被割断的君主，站在制衡之网的外面。

normal.en: Absolutely is the everyday child: it means completely, and also a firm yes.
normal.cn: absolutely 是日常最常用的孩子：它表示「完全」，也表示干脆的「当然」。

normal.en: The grammar term absolute phrase shows the same release: the phrase is free of the main clause's grammar.
normal.cn: 语法术语 absolute phrase 显示同一种释放：这个短语不受主句语法的约束。

abstract.en: Picture a package with every string untied: what remains is the thing itself, not its relations.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包裹，所有绳子都解开了：剩下的就是东西本身，而不是它的各种关系。

abstract.en: From that picture come total qualities, unlimited power, fixed values, and the philosophical Absolute.
abstract.cn: 从这个画面衍生出完全的性质、无限的权力、固定的数值，以及哲学上的绝对者。

abstract.en: Every sense answers one question: is anything outside this thing still able to limit it?
abstract.cn: 每个义项都在回答一个问题：这个东西之外，还有别的东西能限制它吗？

examples.en: The room was in absolute darkness.
examples.cn: 房间里一片漆黑。

examples.en: The king held absolute power over the region.
examples.cn: 国王对该地区拥有绝对权力。

examples.en: The vote gave the party an absolute majority.
examples.cn: 这次投票让该党获得了绝对多数。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布索鲁特」——阿布说话从不加条件，一句就是全部

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ solvere（松开）→ absolvere「解开、免除」→ 分词 absolutus「被解除约束的、完成的」。经法语进入英语后，由「免除义务」发展出「完全的、不受限制的」，再进入科学（绝对零度）、政治（绝对权力）与哲学（绝对者）。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses describe what has no limit and no comparison: completeness, unchecked power, the non-relative, the certain, and an extreme value.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项描述没有限度、不可比较的东西：完全、权力不受限、非相对、确实无疑，以及极值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ropes untied and falling away from a package.
core.cn: 核心意象：绳索被解开，从包裹上滑落。

branches.en: THE COMPLETENESS: nothing is left out.
branches.cn: 完全线：一点也没有剩下。

branches.en: THE POWER: no one stands above it.
branches.cn: 权力线：没有谁在它之上。

branches.en: THE NON-RELATIVE: it is not measured against anything else.
branches.cn: 绝对线：它不拿别的东西来比。

branches.en: THE CERTAINTY: no doubt remains.
branches.cn: 确证线：不再有疑问。

branches.en: THE EXTREME: a scale reaches its end point.
branches.cn: 极值线：刻度走到尽头。

intro.cn: absolute 由一个拉丁前缀和一个拉丁动词构成，同样的构件反复出现在它的词族里。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is solvere, absolvere, and absolutus, with the prefix ab- meaning away.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 solvere、absolvere 与 absolutus；前缀 ab- 意为「离开」。

items.example: It marks release in absolute and absolve.
items.exampleCN: 它在 absolute 与 absolve 中表示释放。

items.example: It also gives solve and dissolve.
items.exampleCN: 它还产生 solve 与 dissolve。

items.example: It is the direct source of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族的直接来源。

items.example: French absolu comes from this form.
items.exampleCN: 法语 absolu 出自这个形式。

items.example: It entered English from French.
items.exampleCN: 它从法语进入英语。

items.example: You are absolutely right.
items.exampleCN: 你完全说得对。

items.example: The century is known for royal absolutism.
items.exampleCN: 那个世纪以王权专制著称。

items.example: It turns absolute into absolutely.
items.exampleCN: 它把 absolute 变成 absolutely。

definition_zh: 吸收；吸进；使专注；缓冲；承担；并入
definition_en: to take in a liquid, gas, energy, or knowledge, or to hold someone's full attention
core_image: 一块干海绵放进水里，水从四周被吸进去
scene: 毛巾铺在洒出的水上，几秒钟就把液体全吸了进去。The dry soil absorbed the rain within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 absorbed 指土壤吸进雨水（第 1 个义项：吸收液体）；句意为干土几分钟内就把雨水吸干了。

pos.zh: 吸收；吸进；使专注；缓冲；承担；并入

derivatives.zh: 由词根加 -tion 构成，义为「吸收；专注；合并」
由动词加 -ent 构成，义为「能吸水的；吸收性的」
由 absorbent 加 -y 构成，义为「吸收能力」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「引人入胜的」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「吸收器；减震器」

senses.title: To take in a liquid or gas
senses.definition: to take a liquid or gas into itself, so that it becomes part of the material
senses.definitionCN: 把液体或气体吸入自身，使其成为材料的一部分
senses.example: The cloth absorbed the spilled milk.
senses.exampleCN: 布把洒出的牛奶吸干了。
senses.why: Latin sorbere meant to suck in, and the prefix ab- adds the idea of drawing something away into oneself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sorbere 意为「吸进」，前缀 ab- 又加上「把某物拉走、纳入自身」的意思。

senses.title: To take in energy
senses.definition: to receive and hold energy such as light, heat, or sound instead of letting it pass through
senses.definitionCN: 接收并留住光、热、声等能量，而不是让其穿过
senses.example: Dark surfaces absorb more heat than light ones.
senses.exampleCN: 深色表面比浅色表面吸收更多热量。
senses.why: Energy enters the material and does not leave, which is the same inward movement as a sponge taking water.
senses.whyCN: 能量进入材料后没有离开，这与海绵吸水的向内运动是一样的。

senses.title: To hold someone's full attention
senses.definition: to interest someone so completely that they notice nothing else
senses.definitionCN: 使某人极感兴趣，以至于注意不到其他事物
senses.example: The novel absorbed her for the whole afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小说让她整个下午都沉浸其中。
senses.why: Attention is imagined as a liquid that the mind drinks, leaving no room for anything else.
senses.whyCN: 注意力被想象成一种被头脑饮下的液体，没给其他事物留下空间。

senses.title: To take in knowledge
senses.definition: to learn and retain information or ideas gradually
senses.definitionCN: 逐步学会并留住信息或观念
senses.example: Children absorb languages faster than adults.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童掌握语言比成人快。
senses.why: The mind is treated as a porous material, and knowledge as something that soaks in rather than is poured on.
senses.whyCN: 头脑被当作多孔的材料，知识是被吸进去的，而不是浇在表面的。

senses.title: To cushion an impact
senses.definition: to reduce the force of a blow or shock by taking it into oneself
senses.definitionCN: 通过把冲击纳入自身来削弱其力量
senses.example: The soft floor absorbed the force of the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 松软的地面吸收了坠落的力量。
senses.why: A cushion absorbs energy and gives it out slowly, so the blow never reaches what lies behind it.
senses.whyCN: 缓冲垫吸收能量再慢慢释放，于是冲击永远到不了它后面的东西。

senses.title: To take on a cost or loss
senses.definition: to pay for or accept a cost that would otherwise fall on someone else
senses.definitionCN: 支付或接受原本会落到别人身上的费用
senses.example: The company absorbed the extra shipping costs.
senses.exampleCN: 公司承担了额外的运费。
senses.why: Money, like water, is pictured as flowing into the firm's body so that customers do not feel it.
senses.whyCN: 钱像水一样被想象成流进公司的身体，好让顾客感觉不到。

senses.title: To incorporate or merge
senses.definition: to take in a smaller group or unit so that it becomes part of a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 把较小的群体或单位纳入，使其成为更大单位的一部分
senses.example: The district was absorbed into the neighbouring city.
senses.exampleCN: 这个区被并入邻近的城市。
senses.why: When a town is absorbed, its separate outline disappears into the larger body, as water disappears into cloth.
senses.whyCN: 一个镇被并入时，它独立的轮廓消失在更大的身体里，就像水消失在布里。

intro.en: Absorb is Latin for sucking something away into oneself, and its family of senses all describe a one-way inward movement.
intro.cn: absorb 在拉丁语中意为「把某物吸走、纳入自身」，它的一族义项都描写单向的向内运动。

items.en: Modern English absorbs liquids, energy, attention, knowledge, costs, and whole organisations, all by the same inward image.
items.cn: 现代英语用它吸收液体、能量、注意力、知识、费用乃至整个组织，全靠同一个向内的画面。

items.en: Early experimenters used the word for materials that take in liquid or gas and for bodies that take in light and heat.
items.cn: 早期的实验者用这个词指吸入液体或气体的材料，也指吸光吸热的物体。

items.en: English borrowed the verb from French absorber in the fifteenth century, at first for liquids and sponges.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪从法语 absorber 借入这个动词，最初用于液体与海绵。

items.en: Absorbere joined ab, away, with sorbere, to suck in, giving the picture of drinking something up.
items.cn: absorbere 把表示离开的 ab 与表示吸进的 sorbere 组合起来，画面就是把东西喝干。

items.en: Sorbere meant to suck or swallow and is also behind the English word sorbet through a different path.
items.cn: sorbere 意为「吸、吞」，经由另一条路径也进入了英语的 sorbet 一词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and nouns from the same absorbing root; the near-meaning group collects verbs for soaking, engrossing, and merging.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「吸收」词根的形式与名词；近义组收表示浸吸、吸引与合并的动词。

entries.definition: The act of taking something in, or deep attention.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸收；专注；合并」。

entries.definition: Able to take in liquid easily.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能吸水的；吸收性的」。

entries.definition: The ability of a material to take in liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「吸收能力」。

entries.definition: To hold molecules on a surface rather than inside a material.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸附」，指分子附着在表面而非进入内部，词形与 absorb 相近。

entries.definition: To make something wet through by leaving it in liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「浸泡；浸透」。

entries.definition: To draw liquid into the mouth by creating a vacuum.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「吸；吮」。

entries.definition: To hold all of someone's attention.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使全神贯注」。

entries.definition: To take in and make part of a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「同化；吸收并纳入」。

entries.definition: To soften the effect of a blow or shock.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「缓冲；减轻冲击」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin sucking picture and the everyday situations where absorption happens.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用拉丁语「吸」的画面，以及吸收发生的日常情境。

normal.en: Ab plus sorb: sorb means to suck, so absorb is to suck something away into yourself.
normal.cn: ab 加 sorb：sorb 意为吸，所以 absorb 就是把东西吸进自己体内。

normal.en: A sponge is the model of the first sense: put it down, and the puddle disappears upward.
normal.cn: 海绵是第一个义项的模型：把它放下去，水洼就往上消失了。

normal.en: When a book absorbs you, your attention is the puddle and the book is the sponge.
normal.cn: 当一本书 absorb 你，你的注意力就是水洼，书就是海绵。

normal.en: Absorption is the noun, absorbent is the material, absorbency is how much it can take.
normal.cn: absorption 是名词，absorbent 是材料，absorbency 是它能吸多少。

normal.en: Adsorb is the technical cousin: same sound, but molecules stay on the surface.
normal.cn: adsorb 是技术上的近亲：读音相近，但分子只留在表面。

abstract.en: Picture a dry cloth laid over a spill: the liquid moves in one direction and does not come back.
abstract.cn: 想象一块干布铺在洒出的液体上：液体单向移动，不再回来。

abstract.en: Every sense keeps that one-way flow: water, heat, attention, knowledge, cost, or a whole town.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都保留这条单向流动：水、热、注意力、知识、费用，甚至一整座镇。

abstract.en: The word is about being taken in, not about being destroyed.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的是「被吸纳」，而不是「被消灭」。

examples.en: The dry soil absorbed the rain within minutes.
examples.cn: 干土几分钟内就把雨水吸干了。

examples.en: She was completely absorbed in her work.
examples.cn: 她完全沉浸在工作中。

examples.en: The company absorbed the extra costs.
examples.cn: 公司承担了额外的成本。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ sorbere（吸、吞）→ absorbere「吸走、吞入」；经法语 absorber 进入英语。核心是单向的向内运动：液体、能量、注意力、知识、费用乃至整个组织，都被纳入更大的身体。

sensesIntro.en: Seven senses take something in: liquid, energy, attention, knowledge, shock, cost, and finally a smaller unit into a larger one.
sensesIntro.cn: 七个义项都是「把某物收进来」：液体、能量、注意力、知识、冲击、成本，最后是较小的单位并入较大的整体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dry sponge taking water upward into itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块干海绵把水向上吸进自身。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: a surface or body takes in liquid, light, sound or heat.
branches.cn: 物质线：表面或物体吸入液体、光、声或热。

branches.en: THE MIND: attention and knowledge are taken in the same way.
branches.cn: 心智线：注意力与知识也以同样的方式被收进来。

branches.en: THE SHOCK: the blow is taken and softened.
branches.cn: 缓冲线：冲击被接住并减弱。

branches.en: THE COST: the loss is taken onto one's own account.
branches.cn: 成本线：损失被记到自己账上。

branches.en: THE UNIT: a smaller thing is swallowed into a larger one.
branches.cn: 同化线：较小的东西被并入较大的整体。

intro.en: Absorb is a Latin verb made of a prefix of separation and a verb of sucking.
intro.cn: absorb 是一个拉丁动词，由表示分离的前缀与表示吸的动词构成。

latinIntro.en: The recorded forms are sorbere, absorbere, and absorptio; the prefix ab- means away.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的形式是 sorbere、absorbere 与 absorptio；前缀 ab- 意为「离开」。

items.example: It marks drawing away in absorb.
items.exampleCN: 它在 absorb 中表示「吸走」。

items.example: It supplies the physical picture.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了具体的画面。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: It gives English absorption.
items.exampleCN: 它产生了英语的 absorption。

items.example: It entered English through French.
items.exampleCN: 它经法语进入英语。

items.example: It forms absorption.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absorption。

items.example: It forms absorbent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 absorbent。

items.exampleCN: 它可作形容词使用。

definition_zh: 抽象的；理论上的；摘要；提取
definition_en: existing as an idea rather than a physical thing, or a short summary, or to remove something from a larger whole
core_image: 从一堆具体的东西里抽出一根线，只剩下骨架
scene: 画家先把桌上的苹果、瓶子和桌布全部省去，只留下几道交错的线。The abstract painting showed shapes with no recognizable objects.
sceneCN: 这里 abstract 指不描绘具体物象的绘画（第 2 个义项：抽象艺术）；句意为这幅抽象画只有形状，没有可辨认的物体。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「抽象；抽象概念；提取」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「抽象地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「抽象性」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「心不在焉的；出神的」
由 abstraction 加 -ism 构成，义为「抽象主义」

senses.title: Existing as an idea, not a physical thing
senses.definition: existing as a thought or quality rather than as an object you can touch
senses.definitionCN: 以思想或性质的形式存在，而不是可触的实物
senses.example: Justice is an abstract idea.
senses.exampleCN: 正义是一种抽象观念。
senses.why: Latin abstrahere meant to draw away, and an idea is what remains when the physical details are drawn off.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abstrahere 意为「抽走」，观念就是抽掉具体细节后剩下的东西。

senses.title: Art without recognisable objects
senses.definition: describing art that uses shapes, colours, and lines instead of copying real things
senses.definitionCN: 指用形状、色彩与线条而不摹写实物的艺术
senses.example: Kandinsky was a pioneer of abstract art.
senses.exampleCN: 康定斯基是抽象艺术的先驱。
senses.why: The painter performs the same act as the word: the object is drawn away, and the pattern is left.
senses.whyCN: 画家做的是和这个词一样的动作：把物体抽走，留下图案。

senses.title: A short summary of a paper
senses.definition: a brief statement at the head of an article that summarises its argument
senses.definitionCN: 放在文章开头、概括其论点的简短陈述
senses.example: Read the abstract before the full paper.
senses.exampleCN: 先读摘要，再读全文。
senses.why: A summary is the essence extracted from the paper, on the same model as a chemical extract.
senses.whyCN: 摘要是从论文里抽出的精华，其模型与化学中的提取物相同。

senses.title: To extract a substance
senses.definition: to remove a substance from a mixture, often by a technical process
senses.definitionCN: 从混合物中取出某种物质，常用于技术过程
senses.example: The oil is abstracted from the seeds.
senses.exampleCN: 油是从种子里提取出来的。
senses.why: This is the most physical sense: something is drawn out and separated from the rest.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的义项：某物被抽出来，与其余部分分离。

senses.title: Considered in theory only
senses.definition: in the phrase in the abstract, thinking about an idea apart from real cases
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 in the abstract 中，脱离实际情形去思考一个观念
senses.example: In the abstract, the plan sounds fair.
senses.exampleCN: 从理论上说，这个计划听起来是公平的。
senses.why: To consider in the abstract is to lift the idea out of its examples and look at the shape alone.
senses.whyCN: 在抽象层面考虑，就是把观念从例子里提出来，只看它的形状。

intro.en: Abstract is Latin for drawn away, and its senses move from extracting a substance to extracting an idea.
intro.cn: abstract 在拉丁语中意为「被抽走」，它的义项从提取物质一路走到提取观念。

items.en: Modern English abstracts data, costs, and ideas, and still writes abstracts at the head of papers.
items.cn: 现代英语提取数据、费用与观念，也仍在论文开头写摘要。

items.en: Twentieth-century critics fixed abstract as the label for art that refuses to copy visible objects.
items.cn: 二十世纪的批评家把 abstract 固定为拒绝摹写可见物象的艺术标签。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English borrowed the word from French abstract and used it for summaries and for ideas separated from matter.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语从法语 abstract 借入这个词，用于摘要，也用于脱离物质的概念。

items.en: Latin abstractus was the past participle of abstrahere, meaning drawn away or separated.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abstractus 是 abstrahere 的过去分词，意为「被抽走、被分离」。

items.en: The verb trahere meant to draw or pull and also produced attract, extract, and contract.
items.cn: 动词 trahere 意为「拉、拖」，还产生了 attract、extract、contract 等词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and nouns from the same drawing-away root; the near-meaning group collects words for ideas, summaries, and extraction.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「抽走」词根的形式与名词；近义组收表示观念、摘要与提取的词。

entries.definition: The act of forming an idea, or an idea so formed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抽象；抽象概念」。

entries.definition: In terms of ideas rather than concrete things.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「抽象地」。

entries.definition: Lost in thought, with attention drawn away.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「心不在焉的；出神的」。

entries.definition: An art style built on abstraction.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「抽象主义」。

entries.definition: Based on ideas rather than physical things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「概念上的」。

entries.definition: Concerned with theory rather than practice.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「理论上的」。

entries.definition: A short account of the main points.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「摘要；总结」。

entries.definition: To remove something from a larger whole.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提取；取出」。

entries.definition: Not able to be touched or physically grasped.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「无形的；不可触的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin picture of pulling something out and the school and studio phrases the word lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「把东西抽出」的拉丁画面，以及这个词所在的课堂与画室搭配。

normal.en: Abs plus tract: tract means drawn or pulled, so abstract is pulled away from the concrete.
normal.cn: abs 加 tract：tract 意为拉，所以 abstract 就是从具体事物里被拉走。

normal.en: The noun abstract is a paper's extract: the same word serves the lab and the library.
normal.cn: 名词 abstract 是论文的提取物：同一个词同时服务实验室与图书馆。

normal.en: In the abstract means with the cases removed, so only the principle is left standing.
normal.cn: in the abstract 意为去掉案例，只让原理站着。

normal.en: Abstract art repeats the act literally: the real apple is pulled away, the line remains.
normal.cn: 抽象艺术把这个动作演示出来：真实的苹果被抽走，线留了下来。

normal.en: The grammar term abstract noun labels names you cannot touch, like courage and freedom.
normal.cn: 语法术语 abstract noun 标记那些摸不到名字的东西，如勇气与自由。

abstract.en: Picture a chair with every physical part removed until only the relation of seat and legs remains.
abstract.cn: 想象一把椅子被抽掉所有实体部分，只剩座位与椅腿之间的关系。

abstract.en: That leftover relation is the abstract thing: it can be thought, drawn, and argued about, but not sat on.
abstract.cn: 剩下的这层关系就是抽象之物：可以思考、描绘、争论，却不能坐上去。

abstract.en: Every sense moves along the same line, from pulling out oil to pulling out a principle.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都沿同一条线移动，从抽出油到抽出原理。

examples.en: Her abstract paintings avoid recognisable objects.
examples.cn: 她的抽象画避开可辨认的物体。

examples.en: He wrote a short abstract of the paper.
examples.cn: 他为这篇论文写了一则短摘要。

examples.en: In the abstract, the scheme sounds reasonable.
examples.cn: 从理论上说，这个方案听起来合理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿布斯特拉克特」——阿布把具体的东西全抽走，只剩一副骨架

root: 拉丁语 abs-（离开）+ trahere（拉、抽）→ abstrahere「抽走、分离」→ 分词 abstractus。经法语进入英语：具体义为「提取」，观念义为「从实物中抽出的性质」，艺术义为「抽掉物象的画法」。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses move from the non-physical, to abstract art, a summary, the extraction of a substance, and purely theoretical thought.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项从非实体的东西，走到抽象艺术、摘要、提取物质，以及纯理论的思考。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line pulled out of a bundle, leaving a bare frame.
core.cn: 核心意象：从一捆东西里抽出一根线，只剩一副空架。

branches.en: THE CONCEPT: what exists only as an idea.
branches.cn: 概念线：只作为观念存在的东西。

branches.en: THE ART: shape and colour without a subject.
branches.cn: 艺术线：没有具体题材的形状与色彩。

branches.en: THE SUMMARY: the essence pulled out of a paper.
branches.cn: 摘要线：从论文里抽出的要点。

branches.en: THE EXTRACTION: a substance drawn out of a mixture.
branches.cn: 提取线：从混合物里抽出某种物质。

branches.en: THE THEORY: a question considered apart from examples.
branches.cn: 理论线：脱离实例来考虑的问题。

intro.en: Abstract is built from a Latin prefix and the verb to draw, and the parts recur in a large family.
intro.cn: abstract 由一个拉丁前缀与表示「拉」的动词构成，构件在一个庞大的词族里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is trahere, abstrahere, and abstractus; the prefix ab- here marks separation.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 trahere、abstrahere 与 abstractus；前缀 ab- 在这里表示分离。

items.example: It marks separation in abstract.
items.exampleCN: 它在 abstract 中表示分离。

items.example: It also gives extract and attract.
items.exampleCN: 它还产生 extract 与 attract。

items.example: It is the direct source of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词的直接来源。

items.example: French abstrait comes from it.
items.exampleCN: 法语 abstrait 出自它。

items.example: It works as adjective, noun, and verb.
items.exampleCN: 它可作形容词、名词与动词。

items.example: It forms abstraction.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstraction。

items.example: It forms abstractly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstractly。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 abstractionism。

抽象地

definition_zh: 荒谬的；荒唐的；可笑的；不合常理的
definition_en: so unreasonable or illogical that it seems laughable
core_image: 一个人一本正经地做一件根本讲不通的事
scene: 他举着伞站在雨里，却把伞面朝下扣在头顶。It seemed absurd to carry an umbrella upside down in a storm.
sceneCN: 这里 absurd 指行为荒唐可笑（第 1 个义项：荒谬可笑）；句意为在暴风雨里把伞倒着拿，实在荒唐。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「荒谬；荒唐事」
由形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「荒唐地；离谱地」
由形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「荒谬性」
由形容词加 -ism 构成，义为「荒诞主义」
由 absurdism 派生，义为「荒诞派作家或作品」

senses.title: So unreasonable as to be laughable
senses.definition: so clearly against reason that it makes people laugh or shake their heads
senses.definitionCN: 明显违背理性，让人发笑或摇头
senses.example: The plan was absurd from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划从一开始就荒谬。
senses.why: Latin absurdus described something out of tune, and a claim out of tune with reason sounds wrong to the ear.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 absurdus 描写「走调」的东西，与理性走调的说法听起来就不对。

senses.title: Contrary to common sense
senses.definition: opposed to what ordinary experience says must be true
senses.definitionCN: 与日常经验认定的必然情况相反
senses.example: It is absurd to expect a reply in an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 指望一小时内有回复是违背常理的。
senses.why: Common sense is the tuning fork, and whatever cannot match its note is absurd.
senses.whyCN: 常识是那把音叉，对不上它音高的东西就是荒谬的。

senses.title: Theatre of the Absurd
senses.definition: a style of drama showing human life as meaningless and comic
senses.definitionCN: 把人生表现为无意义又滑稽的戏剧风格
senses.example: Beckett's plays belong to the Theatre of the Absurd.
senses.exampleCN: 贝克特的戏剧属于荒诞派戏剧。
senses.why: The movement took the word's sense of broken logic and made it a whole stage world.
senses.whyCN: 这个流派借用了这个词「逻辑断裂」的含义，把它变成一个完整的舞台世界。

senses.title: Reductio ad absurdum
senses.definition: a proof that refutes a claim by showing its consequences to be absurd
senses.definitionCN: 通过展示某个主张的后果荒谬来驳倒它
senses.example: The argument ends in a reductio ad absurdum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证以归谬收场。
senses.why: Logic uses the word as a tool: push the opponent's rule until it produces its own absurd note.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把这个词当工具：把对方的规则推到它自己发出荒谬音高的地方。

intro.en: Absurd is Latin for out of tune, and its modern senses keep that musical idea of a note that does not fit.
intro.cn: absurd 在拉丁语中意为「走调」，它的现代义项都保留着「音符不合调」的音乐观念。

items.en: Modern English uses absurd for bad arguments, comic mismatches, and the human condition alike.
items.cn: 现代英语用 absurd 兼指糟糕的论证、滑稽的不相称与人的处境。

items.en: Twentieth-century drama gave the word a stage: plays in which logic itself breaks down.
items.cn: 二十世纪的戏剧给了这个词一个舞台：逻辑本身崩坏的戏。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English took the word from French absurde, mostly for statements that contradict reason.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语从法语 absurde 借入这个词，主要用于违背理性的陈述。

items.en: Latin absurdus meant out of tune or harsh-sounding, and by extension senseless.
items.cn: 拉丁语 absurdus 意为「走调的、刺耳的」，引申为「没有意义的」。

items.en: The second element is surdus, deaf or dull; scholars debate how exactly deafness produced the sense of discord.
items.cn: 第二个构件是 surdus「聋的、迟钝的」；学者对「聋」如何产生「不和谐」义仍有争论。

note.cn: 形近组收同一「走调」词根的形式与名词；近义组收表示可笑与不合逻辑的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the musical idea of a note out of tune and the stages where the word became famous.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「音符走调」的音乐观念，以及这个词成名的舞台。

normal.en: Ab plus surd: surd means deaf or dull, so absurd is a note the ear refuses to accept.
normal.cn: ab 加 surd：surd 意为聋的、迟钝的，所以 absurd 是耳朵拒绝接受的音符。

normal.en: Imagine an orchestra where one cello plays a different song: that clash is absurd.
normal.cn: 想象一支乐队里有一把大提琴在拉另一首曲子：那种冲突就是荒谬。

normal.en: An absurd plan is a plan tuned to a different key from reality.
normal.cn: 荒唐的计划，就是调到与现实不同调的计划。

normal.en: The Theatre of the Absurd put the wrong note on stage for a whole evening.
normal.cn: 荒诞派戏剧把那个错音搬上舞台，演了一整晚。

normal.en: Reductio ad absurdum is logic's way of letting an argument play its own wrong note.
normal.cn: 归谬法是逻辑学让论证自己奏出那个错音的办法。

abstract.en: Picture two instruments playing the same tune in different keys: nothing is broken, yet nothing fits.
abstract.cn: 想象两件乐器用不同的调演奏同一支曲子：什么都没坏，却什么都合不上。

abstract.en: Every sense is that misfit: words, plans, pairs of objects, whole philosophies.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是这种不合：词语、计划、成对的东西、整套哲学。

abstract.en: The word does not say wrong; it says out of tune.
abstract.cn: 这个词说的不是「错」，而是「走调」。

examples.en: The court called the rule absurd.

branches.en: THE STAGE: a theatre built on meaninglessness.

branches.en: THE LOGIC: a method that drives an idea to its ridiculous end.
branches.cn: 逻辑线：把一个想法推到可笑尽头的方法。

branches.en: THE CONFLICT: what is absurd is always a clash between expectation and fact.

senses.title: A very large quantity
senses.definition: a quantity of something that is much greater than usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 某物的数量远超平常或预期
senses.example: The region has an abundance of fresh water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个地区有大量淡水。
senses.why: Latin abundare meant to overflow, and the noun names the state of a place that has spilled over with something.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abundare 意为「溢流」，这个名词命名的是一个被某物漫出来的状态。

senses.title: A plentiful supply for needs
senses.definition: enough of something to meet every need, with plenty left over
senses.definitionCN: 某物足以满足所有需要，还剩下很多
senses.example: They farmed in an abundance of good soil.
senses.exampleCN: 他们耕作在肥沃土壤充足的地方。
senses.why: The word does not merely count; it measures against need and finds the need covered.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只是计数；它以需要为尺度，并且发现需要已被覆盖。

senses.title: In the phrase in abundance
senses.definition: existing or available in large amounts, as in the fixed phrase
senses.definitionCN: 以大量存在或可获得，见于固定短语
senses.example: Wild flowers grow here in abundance.
senses.exampleCN: 野花在这里大量生长。
senses.why: The preposition turns the noun into an adverb of quantity: the place is simply overflowing.
senses.whyCN: 介词把这个名词变成数量副词：那个地方就是在往外溢。

intro.en: Abundance comes from a Latin verb for overflowing, and the image of water spilling over its banks runs through every sense.
intro.cn: abundance 出自拉丁语中表示「溢出」的动词，水漫过岸的画面贯穿所有义项。

items.en: Modern English uses the noun for food, resources, data, isotopes, and states of mind, always with the idea of more than enough.
items.cn: 现代英语用这个名词指食物、资源、数据、同位素与心态，始终带着「多于所需」的观念。

items.en: Ecologists adopted abundance as a technical measure of how many individuals of a species live in an area.
items.cn: 生态学家采用 abundance 作为技术指标，衡量某物种在一个区域内有多少个体。

items.en: Middle English borrowed the word through French and used it for plentiful harvests and generous supplies.
items.cn: 中古英语经法语借入这个词，用于丰收与充足的供应。

items.en: Latin abundantia was a noun of state built on the verb abundare, meaning to overflow or be rich in something.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abundantia 是由动词 abundare 构成的状态名词，意为「溢出、富于某物」。

items.en: The verb undare meant to rise in waves, from unda, a wave, so abundance pictures a flood rather than a pile.
items.cn: 动词 undare 意为「涌起波浪」，出自 unda「波浪」，所以 abundance 的画面是洪水而不是堆垛。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words from the same overflowing root; the near-meaning group collects nouns for plenty and excess.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「溢出」词根的词；近义组收表示充裕与过量的名词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin wave-and-flood picture and the fixed phrases where the word actually appears.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用拉丁语「波浪与洪水」的画面，以及这个词实际出现的固定短语。

normal.en: Ab plus unda plus nce: unda is a wave, so abundance is a place where something waves over the brim.
normal.cn: ab 加 unda 加 nce：unda 是波浪，所以 abundance 就是某物漫过边沿的地方。

normal.en: Think of a granary whose door is opened: the grain does not stack, it pours.
normal.cn: 想象一扇被打开的粮仓门：谷物不是堆着，而是往外倒。

normal.en: In abundance is the adverbial form: the place is overflowing, not the container.
normal.cn: in abundance 是副词形式：溢出的是地方，不是容器。

normal.en: Natural abundance is the word in a lab coat: how much of an isotope nature supplies.
normal.cn: natural abundance 是穿实验服的这个词：自然界提供多少某种同位素。

normal.en: An abundance mentality is the flood moved into the mind, where there is always enough to share.
normal.cn: abundance mentality 是洪水搬进了心里，那里总有足够的东西可以分享。

abstract.en: Picture a river after rain: the water does not stop at the bank, it goes over it.
abstract.cn: 想象雨后的河流：水不停在岸边，而是漫过岸去。

abstract.en: Every sense measures that overflow, whether the flood is grain, money, isotopes, detail, or confidence.
abstract.cn: 每个义项衡量的都是这种溢出，无论溢出的是谷物、钱、同位素、细节还是信心。

abstract.en: The opposite of the word is not zero but scarcity, the fear that the bank will be dry.
abstract.cn: 这个词的反面不是零，而是稀缺，是担心岸边会干涸。

items.en: Modern English applies abundant to fish, minerals, rain, evidence, and wildlife, always measuring abundance against need.

items.en: Sixteenth-century English borrowed the adjective from French and used it for crops, harvests, and generous nature.

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富于……的；丰富的」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the same overflowing-bank picture and the nouns this adjective most often describes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用同一个「漫岸」画面，以及这个形容词最常修饰的名词。

normal.en: Ab plus unda plus ant: the wave keeps rising until it runs over the edge.
normal.cn: ab 加 unda 加 ant：波浪不断升高，直到漫过边沿。

normal.en: Abundant rain is the picture at its most literal: water coming down faster than the ground can take.
normal.cn: abundant rain 是最字面的画面：水落得比地面吸收得快。

normal.en: Abundant evidence means the proof has overflowed the question.
normal.cn: abundant evidence 意为证据已经漫过了问题本身。

normal.en: The adverb abundantly measures clarity: it is abundantly clear means certainty has overflowed.
normal.cn: 副词 abundantly 衡量清晰度：it is abundantly clear 意为确定性已经溢出。

normal.en: Learn it with in: a land abundant in oil has oil overflowing into it.
normal.cn: 连着 in 一起记：a land abundant in oil 就是石油溢进这片土地。

abstract.en: Picture a cup under a tap that will not close: the cup is not full, it is overflowing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只杯子放在关不掉的水龙头下：杯子不是满了，而是在往外溢。

abstract.en: Whether the flow is fish, rain, minerals, or proof, the adjective says the same thing: too much to count comfortably.
abstract.cn: 无论流出来的是鱼、雨、矿物还是证据，这个形容词说的都是同一件事：多到不必细数。

abstract.en: The word praises quantity, but its picture is motion, not storage.
abstract.cn: 这个词称赞的是数量，但它的画面是流动，而不是储藏。

examples.en: Fish are abundant in this river.
examples.cn: 这条河里的鱼很多。

examples.en: The region has abundant rainfall in summer.
examples.cn: 这个地区夏季降雨充沛。

examples.en: There is abundant evidence for the claim.
examples.cn: 这一主张有充分的证据。

root: 拉丁语 abundare「溢出、富于」的现在分词 abundans → 形容词 abundant。词根 unda 意为「波浪」，ab- 表示向外，画面是水不断涌来、漫过边沿。凡数量多到超出所需，皆可用这个词形容。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses describe a large number, a rich content of something, and a supply that exceeds need.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项描述数量众多、富含某种成分，以及供应超过所需。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water rising until it runs over the bank.
core.cn: 核心意象：水不断上涨，直到漫过河岸。

branches.en: THE NUMBER: many of a kind.
branches.cn: 数量线：同类的东西很多。

branches.en: THE CONTENT: rich in a particular element.
branches.cn: 成分线：某种成分含量丰富。

branches.en: THE SURPLUS: more than is needed.
branches.cn: 余量线：多过所需。

branches.en: THE WEALTH: plenty of things and plenty of one thing share a full measure.
branches.cn: 丰盛线：东西多与某物多，共用同一把满尺。

branches.en: THE ENOUGH: abundance ends in having to spare.
branches.cn: 富余线：丰盛最后落在有所剩余。

intro.en: Abundant is the participial adjective of a Latin verb of overflowing, with a suffix that marks ongoing state.
intro.cn: abundant 是一个拉丁「溢出」动词的分词形容词，后缀表示持续的状态。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is unda, undare, abundare, and abundans.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 unda、undare、abundare 与 abundans。

items.example: It marks overflow in abundare.
items.exampleCN: 它在 abundare 中表示溢出。

items.example: It supplies the flood picture.
items.exampleCN: 它提供了洪水的意象。

items.example: It is the verb behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族背后的动词。

items.example: Its participle gives abundant.
items.exampleCN: 它的分词产生了 abundant。

items.example: It is the direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个形容词的直接来源。

items.example: It came through French.
items.exampleCN: 它经法语进入英语。

items.example: It forms abundant from a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成 abundant。

items.example: Ideas abound in the book.
items.exampleCN: 这本书里观点很多。

definition_zh: 滥用；虐待；辱骂；弊端
definition_en: to use something wrongly or cruelly, or to speak to someone in a harmful way
core_image: 一件本该善用的工具，被握在手里乱砍
scene: 他拿一把本该切菜的刀去撬门锁，刀刃很快就卷了。The manager abused his position to favour a friend.
sceneCN: 这里 abused 指滥用职权（第 1 个义项：滥用权力）；句意为经理滥用职位偏袒朋友。

derivatives.zh: 由词根加 -ive 构成，义为「辱骂的；虐待的」
由 abusive 加 -ly 构成，义为「辱骂地；虐待地」
由 abusive 加 -ness 构成，义为「辱骂性；虐待性」
由动词加 -er 构成，义为「施虐者；滥用者」

senses.title: Misuse of power or position
senses.definition: to use an office or authority for a purpose it was not given for
senses.definitionCN: 把职位或权力用于它本不该服务的目的
senses.example: The official abused his power to award contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 这名官员滥用权力批出合同。
senses.why: Latin abuti meant to use up or use wrongly, and power used for the wrong end is exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 abuti 意为「用尽或用错」，权力被用于错误目的正是如此。

senses.title: Wrong use of a substance
senses.definition: to take a drug or drink in a way that harms the body or mind
senses.definitionCN: 以损害身心的方法使用药物或饮酒
senses.example: He abused painkillers after the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 事故之后他滥用了止痛药。
senses.why: Here the tool is a medicine, and the harm comes from using it outside its purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这里的工具是药物，伤害来自把它用在用途之外。

senses.title: Cruel treatment of a person
senses.definition: to treat a person or animal with violence or neglect
senses.definitionCN: 以暴力或忽视对待人或动物
senses.example: The children had been abused for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这些孩子多年来一直受虐待。
senses.why: The word moves from misusing an object to misusing a person, as if a person were a thing to be used.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「用错东西」转到「用错人」，仿佛把人当成了可供使用的东西。

senses.title: Insulting language
senses.definition: to speak to someone with words meant to hurt or humiliate
senses.definitionCN: 用意在伤害或羞辱的言语对人说话
senses.example: The driver shouted abuse at the cyclist.
senses.exampleCN: 司机对着骑车的人大声辱骂。
senses.why: Language is another tool, and turning it into a weapon is the verbal form of the same misuse.
senses.whyCN: 语言也是一件工具，把它变成武器，就是同一种滥用的言语形式。

senses.title: Abuse of trust
senses.definition: to betray the confidence another person has placed in you
senses.definitionCN: 背叛他人寄予你的信任
senses.example: The tutor abused the trust of the family.
senses.exampleCN: 这名家教辜负了这家人的信任。
senses.why: Trust is a thing handed over for a good purpose, and the betrayal is its wrongful use.
senses.whyCN: 信任是为正当目的交出的东西，背叛就是把它用错了。

intro.en: Abuse is Latin for using something up or using it wrongly, and every sense is a version of that wrong use.
intro.cn: abuse 在拉丁语中意为「用尽或用错」，每个义项都是这种「用错」的一个版本。

items.en: Modern English abuses power, drugs, systems, trust, and language, and calls standing wrongs abuses.
items.cn: 现代英语滥用权力、药物、制度、信任与语言，也把长期存在的错误称为 abuses。

items.en: Social and legal services fixed the word in phrases such as child abuse and drug abuse.
items.cn: 社会与法律服务把这个词固定在 child abuse、drug abuse 等说法中。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English borrowed the word from French abuser, first for misuse of office and of language.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语从法语 abuser 借入这个词，最初指滥用职位与语言。

items.en: Latin abusus was the noun for misuse or consumption, formed from the verb abuti.
items.cn: 拉丁语 abusus 是由动词 abuti 构成的名词，意为「误用、耗用」。

items.en: Abuti joined ab, away, with uti, to use, giving the sense of using something away from its proper end.
items.cn: abuti 把表示离开的 ab 与表示使用的 uti 组合起来，意为「把东西用到偏离其正当目的的地方」。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms and nouns from the same misuse root; the near-meaning group collects verbs for mistreatment and misuse.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「误用」词根的形式与名词；近义组收表示虐待与误用的动词。

entries.definition: Using harsh or cruel language or treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「辱骂的；虐待的」。

entries.definition: In a harsh or cruel manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「辱骂地；虐待地」。

entries.definition: A person who mistreats or misuses something or someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「施虐者；滥用者」。

entries.definition: The quality of being abusive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「辱骂性；虐待性」。

entries.definition: To use something wrongly or for the wrong purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「误用；滥用」。

entries.definition: To treat a person or animal badly.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「虐待；苛待」。

entries.definition: To treat someone cruelly or violently.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「虐待」，语气正式。

entries.definition: To speak or act in a way that offends someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「侮辱；冒犯」。

entries.definition: To use someone or something unfairly for one's own gain.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「剥削；利用」。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the picture of a good tool used for a bad purpose and the phrases the word now lives in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子用「好工具被用错地方」的画面，以及这个词现在固定出现的短语。

normal.en: Ab plus use: use taken away from its proper purpose is abuse.
normal.cn: ab 加 use：使用被拉离它的正当目的，就是 abuse。

normal.en: A kitchen knife used to pick a lock is the whole word in one picture.
normal.cn: 一把菜刀被拿去撬锁，就是这个词的完整画面。

normal.en: Drug abuse and child abuse show the word at its most serious.
normal.cn: drug abuse 与 child abuse 显示这个词最严肃的一面。

normal.en: Verbal abuse is the same misuse applied to language instead of a tool.
normal.cn: verbal abuse 是同一种滥用，只是把工具换成了语言。

normal.en: The legal phrase abuse of process shows how formal the word can become.
normal.cn: 法律短语 abuse of process 显示这个词可以正式到什么程度。

abstract.en: Picture a key used to hammer a nail: the key still works, but in the wrong direction.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙被拿去敲钉子：钥匙还是好的，只是方向错了。

abstract.en: Every sense is that wrong direction: power, drugs, people, words, trust, courts, rules, institutions.
abstract.cn: 每个义项都是那个错误方向：权力、药物、人、言语、信任、法院、规则、制度。

abstract.en: The word always implies a proper use that has been betrayed.
abstract.cn: 这个词始终暗示有一种正当用法被辜负了。

examples.en: The manager abused his position to favour a friend.
examples.cn: 经理滥用职位偏袒朋友。

examples.en: He abused painkillers after the accident.
examples.cn: 事故之后他滥用了止痛药。

examples.en: The driver shouted abuse at the cyclist.
examples.cn: 司机对着骑车的人大声辱骂。

root: 拉丁语 ab-（离开）+ uti（使用）→ abuti「用错、用尽」→ 名词 abusus。经法语 abuser 进入英语。核心是「把东西用到偏离正当目的的地方」：权力、药物、人、语言、信任、程序、制度皆可被这样使用。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses cover misuse of power, misuse of a substance, physical mistreatment, verbal insult, and breach of trust.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项覆盖滥用权力、滥用药物、身体虐待、言语辱骂，以及辜负信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a good tool swung in the wrong direction until it is damaged.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件好工具被朝错误方向挥动，直到损坏。

branches.en: THE MISUSE: a right or a substance is used past its purpose.
branches.cn: 滥用线：权利或药物被用得超出本来的用途。

branches.en: THE BODY: mistreatment leaves marks on a person.
branches.cn: 身体线：虐待在人身上留下痕迹。

branches.en: THE VOICE: words are used as weapons.
branches.cn: 言语线：话语被当作武器使用。

branches.en: THE TRUST: a confidence placed in someone is broken.
branches.cn: 信任线：寄托在某人身上的信任被打破。

branches.en: THE BREACH: misuse of a role always betrays what the role was given for.
branches.cn: 背信线：滥用一个角色，总是背叛了这个角色被赋予的用途。

intro.en: Abuse is built from a Latin prefix of departure and the verb to use, with a suffix that turns it into a noun.
intro.cn: abuse 由表示偏离的拉丁前缀、表示使用的动词构成，后缀使它成为名词。

latinIntro.en: The recorded chain is uti, abuti, and abusus; French abuser carried the verb into English.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的链条是 uti、abuti 与 abusus；法语 abuser 把这个动词带入英语。
